articleTitle: Femtosecond technology for optical clocks
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. This talk will describe recent progress toward developing novel femtosecond laser and nonlinear optical components, generating shorter pulses, producing frequency combs at different wavelengths, controlling pulse timing and optical phase, and locking femtosecond lasers with attosecond precision.

articleTitle: Biological processes studied at the single molecule level
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. This tutorial will discuss single molecule fluorescence methods used to observe conformational changes in biological molecules. Topics covered will include a summary of the methods, instrumentation considerations, and selected applications.

articleTitle: Holding single molecules up to the light: the fluctuating enzymes
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Single-molecule experiments have shown that an enzyme is a dynamical entity whose conformation and enzymatic rate undergo constant fluctuation over a broad range of time scales.

articleTitle: Observation of two-dimensional discrete solitons in optically-induced nonlinear photonic lattices
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report the first experimental observation of 2D optical discrete solitons in nonlinear photonic lattices.

articleTitle: Modelling of a novel hollow-core photonic crystal fibre
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A hollow-core photonic crystal fibre that guides light over a broad range of frequencies has been developed. Calculations indicate that guidance is due to a low density of states of the cladding structure near the air line.

articleTitle: 300 attosecond active synchronization of passively mode-locked lasers using balanced cross-correlation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A balanced cross-correlator, the optical equivalent of a balanced microwave phase-detector, is demonstrated. Its use in synchronization of a sub-10 fs Ti:sapphire laser and a 40 fs Cr:forsterite laser yields 300 attoseconds timing jitter measured from 10 mHz to 2.3 MHz.

articleTitle: Bose-Einstein condensation of optically trapped cesium
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Bose-Einstein condensation of cesium atoms is achieved by evaporative cooling using optical trapping techniques. The ability to tune the interactions between the ultracold atoms by an external magnetic field offers intriguing features for potential applications.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optical manipulation of Fano resonances in 2D photonic crystal slabs
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We experimentally demonstrate nonlinear response of 2D photonic crystal Fano resonance. Phase shifts of 20 times FWHM and gains higher than 7 are measured. An analytical model allows us to describe these outstanding experimental features.

articleTitle: Photosynthetic light-harvesting by carotenoids: detection of an intermediate excited state
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present the first direct evidence of an intermediate excited state mediating internal conversion in carotenoids. Transition to this state occurs within /spl ap/50 fs. This result changes the description of the primary step in photosynthesis.

articleTitle: Long-range molecular resonances in a cold Rydberg gas
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have seen spectral evidence for long-range molecular resonances involving pairs of cold Rydberg atoms. We attribute these features to avoided crossings between Rydberg-Rydberg long-range molecular interaction potentials.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity and disorder in two-dimensional fiber arrays
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We experimentally observe diffusive wave propagation in disordered two-dimensional arrays of interacting optical fibers. A weak Kerr nonlinearity can cause an increased mobility, where strong nonlinearity leads to the formation of discrete solitons.

articleTitle: Zero- to one-dimensional transition and Auger recombination in semiconductor quantum rods
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Studies of Auger recombination in size/shape-controlled CdSe nanoparticles reveal that elongated nanocrystals provide almost independent control of the emission wavelength (diameter) and the Auger recombination rate (length). The results suggest that shape control may be the key to developing practical lasing applications.

articleTitle: Quantized Pancharatnam-Berry phase diffractive optics by use of space-variant subwavelength gratings
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Quantized Pancharatnam-Berry phase diffractive optics using computer-generated space-variant subwavelength dielectric grating is presented. We experimentally demonstrated a quantized blazed polarization diffraction grating, as well as polarization-dependent focusing lens for infrared radiation.

articleTitle: Field enhancement and resonance in optical antennas
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Optical antennas are studied as probes for near-field optical microscopy. Finite difference time domain calculations indicate an intensity enhancement of more than 3 orders of magnitude. Optical antennas are fabricated and tested with good agreement between experiment and theory.

articleTitle: Experimental realization of quantum cryptosystem over 87 km
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have successfully implemented telecom-wavelength quantum cryptosystem over 87.5 km (world's longest) including error correction and privacy amplification. We confirmed that key distribution was performed at a rate of 7.2 bps with a 7.6% QBER.

articleTitle: Molecular fluorescence in the vicinity of gold nanoparticles
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Lissamine molecules attached to differently sized gold-nanoparticles have been studied using time-resolved spectroscopy. We show that resonant energy transfer and a strong reduction in the molecules' radiative lifetime contribute equally to fluorescence quenching.

articleTitle: Very low losses for TM polarized light in photonic crystal waveguides
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Straight photonic crystal waveguides have been fabricated. Experimentally observed transmission spectra for TE and TM polarizations agree very well with 3D-FDTD simulations. Very low coupling and propagation losses are observed for the TM polarization.

articleTitle: Ultrafast many-body spin interactions in highly excited undoped and n-doped bulk GaAs
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We observe a fundamental difference in the influence of doping electrons and optically excited electrons on the electron g-factor and spin relaxation time T/sub 2/ in undoped and n-doped bulk GaAs.

articleTitle: Single-spatial mode coincidence measurement of photon pairs from a highly nondegenerate PPLN downconverter
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have analyzed the mode structure of the 800-nm signal output from a PPLN parametric downconverter and achieved a signal-conditioned 1600-nm-idler detection probability of 5.2% with single-mode fiber coupling for both outputs.

articleTitle: New lenses for imaging the near field
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A slab of material with refractive index n = -1 behaves like a perfect lens. Here we develop the concept showing how layering the lens can improve resolution in lossy systems, and proposing new lenses with magnified images.

articleTitle: Coherent control of nanoscale localization of ultrafast optical excitation in nanostructures
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We predict and theoretically investigate the unique possibility to control distribution of ultrafast local optical fields in nanosystems in space with nanometer resolution and in time on the femtosecond scale. While the spatial degrees of freedom of the optical radiation do not allow focusing of the light on nanoscale, the temporal degrees of freedom, i.e., phases of excitation femtosecond pulses, are quite efficient functional degrees of freedom that permit one to coherently control the distribution of the energy of local fields, concentrating it at a desired location at certain times. Possible applications of this effect include energy supply and control of ultrafast optical computations in nanostructures, local optical probing of nanosystems, including nanosensors of chemical and biological agents, and nanomodification of surfaces (nano-lithography).

articleTitle: A deep ultraviolet ultrafast source driven by high gain harmonic generation in a free electron laser
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: High-gain harmonic generation has been demonstrated at the shortest wavelength to date (266 nm). Megawatt levels of 89 nm radiation are also produced. Experimental applications of the deep ultraviolet light and FEL issues are discussed.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optical manipulation of Fano resonances in 2d photonle crystal slabs
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We experimentally demonstrate nonlinear response of 2D photonic crystal Fano resonance. Phase shifts of 20 times FWHM and gains higher than 7 are measured. An analytical model allows us to describe these outstanding experimental features.

articleTitle: Spatio-temporal autocorrelation of ultrashort-pulse localized wavepackets
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Few-cycle localized wavepackets were generated from a pulsed Ti:sapphire laser by novel-type refractive and reflective axicons. We demonstrated direct detection of characteristic X-pulse structures of Bessel- and Mathieu-like beams in sub-10-fs range by spatio-temporal autocorrelation.

articleTitle: Femtosecond dynamics of light transmission through sub-wavelength hole arrays in metallic films
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report on the observation of an ultrafast modification of /spl sim/30% in the enhanced transmission through sub-wavelength nanometric apertures in metallic films. It demonstrates the feasibility of nanoscaled femtosecond optical switches.

articleTitle: Damping of electron density Rabi-oscillations and self-induced-transparency in semiconductor quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A non-Markovian quantum kinetic theory of the coupled electron-phonon system in semiconductor quantum dots is used to analyze the nonlinear dipole decoherence and light propagation dynamics for arbitrary pulse strengths and lengths.

articleTitle: Testing the stability of the fine structure constant using the /sup 199/Hg/sup +/ single-ion optical clock
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Measurements of the frequency of the /sup 199/Hg/sup +/ ion optical clock versus the cesium primary standard over a two year period can be interpreted as a stringent test of the stability of the fine structure constant.

articleTitle: Coherent Rayleigh-Brillouin scattering in polyatomic gases
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present experimental data and a well matched theory of the coherent Rayleigh-Brillouin scattering line shape in polyatomic gases. Interactions between optical lattice and thermal gas molecules are discussed.

articleTitle: Jitter and skew reduction using an ultra-fast two-dimensional organic optical switch
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present a femtosecond timing measurement and control technique for jitter or skew reduction using a squarylium dye J-aggregate film as an ultra-fast two-dimensional optical switch. Jitter reduction is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Efficient electron spin detection with positively charged quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Using polarization sensitive time-resolved photoluminescence upconversion experiments, we demonstrate that positively charged quantum dots act as a highly efficient detector for spin polarized electrons in semiconductor heterostructures.

articleTitle: Evanescent coupling from optical fiber tapers to photonic crystal waveguides and resonators
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Using a coupled mode theory and finite-difference time-domain calculations nearly complete evanescent power transfer between a fiber taper and a photonic crystal defect waveguide which is ideal for probing high-Q cavities is predicted.

articleTitle: Delayed-choice quantum cryptography
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Delayed-choice quantum cryptography is a novel protocol, incorporating an optical storage system, which achieves substantially higher effective data rates for quantum key distribution.

articleTitle: Interaction of a light beam with light-induced photonic lattices
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally that the interaction of a light beam with a 2D waveguide lattice induced by partially coherent soliton arrays leads to a host of new phenomena including lattice dislocation, lattice deformation, and creation of structures akin to optical polarons.

articleTitle: Systematic design of directional couplers in photonic crystal
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Systematic design of directional couplers in photonic crystals is considered, and three methods to control the coupling length are proposed. Bending of coupled waveguide is considered and optimum frequency of operation to get efficient waveguide coupling and bending is presented.

articleTitle: Nanooptics on single magnetic semiconductor quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate the ability to monitor the magnetization of a single CdSe/ZnMnSe magnetic quantum dot by means of nano-optical spectroscopy. The average magnetic moment as well as statistical magnetic fluctuations are extracted from our data.

articleTitle: Anomalously fast decay of LH-HH exciton Raman coherence
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Three-beam four-wave mixing measurements of dephasing of the light-hole to heavy-hole exciton Raman coherence in GaAs quantum wells show that it is anomalously fast compared to dephasing of the optical coherences.

articleTitle: Diffraction management and elliptic discrete solitons in two-dimensional waveguide array lattices
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate that the discrete diffraction properties of a 2-D waveguide array can be effectively altered depending on the propagation k-vector within the Brillouin zone of the lattice. In general, this diffraction behavior is anisotropic, and therefore, allows the existence of discrete elliptic solitons.

articleTitle: Correlated influence of carrier-carrier/carrier-phonon interaction and radiative damping on semiconductor intersubband transitions
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The linewidth of intersubband transitions resulting from simultaneous action of many-body contributions and radiative damping is analyzed. The processes are non-additive and a self-consistent treatment is necessary to explain recent experiments.

articleTitle: Photoluminescence from sharp gold tips
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The properties of photoluminescence from gold nanostructures is studied with one and two-photon excitation. By using a tip, the signal is studied spectroscopically under well-defined conditions.

articleTitle: Dynamic nonlinear effect on lasing in random media
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We investigate the dynamic effect of nonlinearity on lasing in disordered medium. The third-order nonlinearity not only changes frequency and size of lasing mode, but also modifies laser emission intensity and laser pulse width.

articleTitle: Solid-state light phase detector
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate a solid-state device capable of unambiguously measuring the carrier-envelope phase of ultrashort (4-femtosecond), low-energy (unamplified) laser pulses using photoelectron emission from a gold surface in the multiphoton regime.

articleTitle: Generation of coherent "water window" soft x-rays using quasi-phase-matching
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate that high-harmonic generation can be phase-matched in the "water window" region of the spectrum using periodically-modulated hollow fibers. We also observe emission from ions.

articleTitle: Coupled mode analysis and demonstration of an electrooptic frequency shifter
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present a semiclassical wave mixing analysis to study the effect of a microwave field on a train of short optical pulses in a traveling wave modulator structure. The devices can achieve long range and continuous shifting. Experimental results from such device will be shown.

articleTitle: Ultrabright tunable photon-pair source with total-flux polarization-entanglement
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate a continuous-wave dual-pump tunable source of polarization-entangled photons that requires no spectral or spatial filtering and emits ten times more pairs per mW of pump than pervious sources.

articleTitle: Observation of superluminal pulse propagation in alexandrite
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We observe superluminal light propagation in an alexandrite crystal. Negative group velocities result from a narrow anti-hole in the homogeneously broadened absorption spectrum. The anti-hole is formed by coherent population oscillations in an inverse-saturable absorber.

articleTitle: Coupling into photonic crystal slab waveguides
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: An adiabatic taper method is presented for coupling light into photonic crystal defect waveguides in a square lattice of circular dielectric rods. The taper consists of two coupling stages.

articleTitle: Nonlinear refraction and absorption from 1300 to 2200 in single crystal polymer poly[bis(p-toluene sulfonate)] of 2, 4-hexadiyne-1, 6-diol (PTS)
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Multi-photon absorption and refraction were measured in polydiacetylene-PTS (p-toluene sulfonate) from 1200 to 2200 nm. The four-photon absorption coefficient peaks at 1900 nm and n/sub 2/ decreases monotonically over this range.

articleTitle: Measurement of photonic band-gap fiber transmission from 1.0 to 3.0 /spl mu/m and impact of surface mode coupling
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report the measurement of a 475-nm wide transmission window of a photonic band-gap fiber using a FT-IR measurement technique. A comparison between measurement and theory demonstrates the impact of surface modes on fiber transmission.

articleTitle: Near-field optical spectroscopy with 20 nm spatial resolution
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A near-field optical method is introduced that makes use of the strongly enhanced electric field close to a sharply pointed metal tip under laser illumination. The tip is held a few nanometers above the sample surface so that a highly localized interaction between the enhanced field and the sample is achieved. The method has been successfully combined with vibrational spectroscopy by making use of the well-known effect of surface enhanced Raman scattering (SERS). We mapped out the vibrational modes of individual single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNT) with a resolution better than 20 nm. The technique has great potential for becoming a routine tool for the chemical analysis of surfaces at high spatial resolution.

articleTitle: Laser cooling thulium-doped glass by 24K from room temperature
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Thulium-doped glass is cooled 24 K below ambient by arranging a Brewster-cut sample in a multiple-pass pump geometry. Modelling based on new spectroscopy data predicts the feasibility of achieving cryogenic temperatures.

articleTitle: 4 states protocol for time coding quantum key distribution
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Coherent one photon pulses are sent with four possible time delays with respect to a reference. Ambiguity of the photon time detection resulting from pulses overlap combined with interferometric measurement allows for secure key exchange.

articleTitle: Ultrafast photoinduced above-bandgap transparency in GaAs due to the dynamic Franz-Keldysh effect
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report the dynamic Franz-Keldysh effect in bulk GaAs. Ultrafast changes in transmission spectra near the band edge, including the first observation of photoinduced transparency as large as 40% are observed.

articleTitle: Observation of multiple soliton generation mediated by amplification of asymmetries
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report the experimental observation of the formation of multiple optical quadratic solitons in a process mediated by the amplification of minute asymmetries in the diffraction properties of the input light.

articleTitle: Dispersion of the nonlinear susceptibility of GaAs in the THz range
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We investigate the nonlinear susceptibility of GaAs via SHG with a free-electron laser below the optical phonon resonance. The observation of a maximum and a zero-crossing allows the quantitative determination of higher-order lattice potentials.

articleTitle: Boundary element method applied to the analysis of the plasmon and phonon response of various nano- and micro-structures
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The boundary element method is used to calculate the plasmon response of metallic nanoparticles having different shapes. Excitation leads to large near-field and scattering amplitude. Comparisons are made with phonon excitation in polar dielectrics.

articleTitle: Multi-band vector solitons in waveguide arrays
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We theoretically present vector solitons in a waveguide array whose components belong to different bands, where light in the first mode is concentrated primarily in the waveguides and the second component is a radiative mode in which light is primarily concentrated in between sites.

articleTitle: Tip-induced polaritonic resonance in scattering-type near-field microscopy
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Apertureless near-field probing induces a resonant response in polaritonic (negative-epsilon) materials, demonstrated in 890-1090 cm/sup -1/ spectra (CO/sub 2/ laser) of (i) plasmon-enhancement by mobile electrons in Si, (ii) plasmon-enhancement by the fundamental lattice vibration of SiC.

articleTitle: Influence of exciton-exciton interaction on the system-size dependence of /spl chi//sup (3)/ at one-exciton resonance
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We theoretically study the influence of the exciton-exciton interaction H/sub ex-ex/ on the system-size dependence of /spl chi//sup (3)/ at one-exciton resonance, which reveals the great enhancement of /spl chi//sup (3)/ at one-exciton resonance induced by H/sub ex-ex/.

articleTitle: Attosecond metrology and spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. This talk will review the recent generation, measurement and first applications of isolated sub-femtosecond soft-X-ray pulses for time-resolved inner-shell spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Development of solid state materials with negative index of refraction and "perfect" lenses
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate that a photonic structure consisting of materials with positive and negative dielectric permittivity can exhibit left-handedness. Examples of plasmonic (Ag) and phononic (SiC) building blocks will be used. SiC is also attractive for a near-field "perfect" lens which dramatically enhances resolution of near-field imaging.

articleTitle: Studies of the mechanism for the formation of the self-trapped exciton in quasi-one-dimensional systems
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We present studies of the vibrational coherence properties of the self-trapped exciton in a quasi-one-dimensional system using femtosecond impulsive excitation techniques.

articleTitle: Optical control of photon tunneling through an array of nanometer scale cylindrical channels
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Photon tunneling gated by light at a different wavelength in an artificially created array of nanometer scale cylindrical channels in a thick gold film is described. This observation suggests the possibility of building a new class of "gated" photon tunneling devices for massive parallel all-optical signal and image processing.

articleTitle: Construction of a non-deterministic 2-photon CNOT gate
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We present progress towards construction of an optical CNOT gate. The gate is predicted to perform all quantum gate operations within the standard coincidence basis paradigm and test the principles of linear optical quantum computation.

articleTitle: Tera-hertz acousto-electric modulation in piezoelectric InGaN/GaN quantum wells using nano acoustic waves
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrated an ultrafast electron distribution modulation up to THz frequency by using nano acoustic waves in InGaN/GaN multiple-quantum-wells. With amplitude-fixed acoustic waves, the electron energy distribution modulation was observed by using femtosecond optical technique.

articleTitle: Femtosecond non-degenerate pump-probe measurements of single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) within an ordered array of nanosize silica spheres
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present preliminary lifetime data of single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) grown within the voids of an ordered array of silica spheres. Non-degenerate pump-probe measurements with /spl lambda//sub pump/ = 400 nm and /spl lambda//sub probe/ = 800 run indicate a decay of 319 /spl plusmn/ 25 fs.

articleTitle: Non-adiabatic nanometric near-field optical chemical vapor deposition using visible light for ultraviolet metal-organic gas source
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Photodissociation using optical near field of diethylzinc becomes non-adiabatic due to the steep spatial gradient of optical power. Therefore, diethylzinc becomes active even for visible light, although it is active only for UV propagating light.

articleTitle: Apertureless near-field fluorescence microscope for biological imaging
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We measured the optical response of fluorescent beads to sharp metallic and semiconducting probes, revealing several underlying near-field interactions. Our results suggest that /spl sim/10 nanometer optical resolution with spectroscopic chemical sensitivity is possible, and bear strongly on molecular-scale biological imaging.

articleTitle: Measurements of the Wigner distribution of non-classical fields in cavity QED
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have measured the Wigner function of the vacuum and of a one photon field state prepared in a high Q cavity. We implement a method proposed by Lutterbach and Davidovich. The field state is prepared in a high Q superconducting microwave cavity and measured by a single circular Rydberg atom which is strongly coupled to the cavity mode. An analysis of the measured Wigner function allows to reconstruct efficiently the actual photon number distribution of the prepared field.

articleTitle: Least-squares technique to determine the second-order nonlinearity of thin films of low symmetry
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We develop a least-squares technique to determine the second-harmonic susceptibility tensor of thin films of low symmetry. The technique avoids the need to calibrate absolute signal levels and allows addressing the quality of various theoretical models.

articleTitle: Ultrafast suppression and recovery of a resonant photonic bandgap
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Resonant photonic bandgap structures, formed by Bragg-spaced quantum wells, are studied experimentally with resonant pump-probe spectroscopy. We find ultrafast suppression due to the ac Stark effect and ultrafast recovery enabled by superradiant decay of the coherent polarization.

articleTitle: Raman enhanced white light continuum generation about the second dispersion zero of the tapered fibers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The nonlinear femtosecond IR-pulse propagation about the zero dispersion wavelength of the tapered fibers is analyzed. A new mechanism of the spectral down-frequency extra-broadening differing from that in the visible range is revealed.

articleTitle: Dependence of the NdSc/sub 3/(BO/sub 3/)/sub 4/ random laser output parameters on the particle size
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: In NdSc/sub 3/(BO/sub 3/)/sub 4/ random laser, we experimentally studied the dependence of the threshold, slope efficiency, and effective photon residence time on the size of powder particles. Optimum lasing conditions are found at medium particle sizes.

articleTitle: Controllable frequency entanglement via auto-phase-matched spontaneous parametric down-conversion
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A new method for generating entangled photons with controllable frequency correlation via spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is presented. The method entails initiating counter-propagating SPDC in a single-mode nonlinear waveguide by pumping with a pulsed beam perpendicular to the waveguide.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional IR/visible measurements of /spl chi//sup 2/
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report on a new class of optical multidimensional Fourier-transform spectroscopy associated with a visible excitation infrared emission configuration, in which the emitted field results from second-order optical nonlinearities.

articleTitle: Strong-field photoionization and absolute phase of few-cycle laser pulses
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present the first experimental evidence for an effect of the absolute phase. Atoms are ionized by a short laser pulse and the electrons leaving the ion core are registered with two detectors facing each other on opposite sides of the laser beam. Thus, each laser pulse can be characterized by the number of electrons emitted to the left and the right. Accordingly, the laser shots are recorded in a contingency map. Due to the absolute phase, a laser shot that produces a lot of electrons flying to the right has a high probability to produce only a few flying to the left. This anticorrelation becomes visible as a structure perpendicular to the diagonal.

articleTitle: Beam shaping by a periodic structure of left-handed slabs
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We analyze the transmission properties of a layered structure consisting of the slabs of positive and negative refractive index materials and demonstrate the unique properties of the beam propagation and shaping.

articleTitle: An experimental investigation of criteria for continuous variable entanglement
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We characterize entangled optical beams using an EPR criterion and an inseparability criterion, and demonstrate qualitative and quantitative differences. We clarify this discrepancy by considering entanglement in terms of necessary and excess sideband photon numbers.

articleTitle: Synthesis of ultrastable femtosecond pulse trains from an optical reference oscillator
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We phase-lock the repetition rates of two Ti:sapphire femtosecond lasers to an optical reference oscillator at their 456000th harmonic and achieve sub-femtosecond timing jitter. A system that can be continuously stabilized for periods approaching one day is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Collapse of a homogeneous Bose-Einstein condensate
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We probe the collapse of large attractive Bose-Einstein condensates. We observe the amplification of a local instability by seeding a momentum state p and switching the scattering length negative via a Feshbach resonance. We also observe the appearance of atoms in the conjugate momentum state.

articleTitle: Analysis of coherent shear waves generation by femtosecond laser pulse in nitride-based MQW
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Based on a macroscopic continuum theory, it is predicted that coherent transverse acoustic (TA) phonons, i.e. shear waves, can be photoexcited by launching femtosecond laser pulse into the InGaN/GaN MQW with general crystal growth directions.

articleTitle: Optical studies of symmetry and spin relaxation in II-VI self-assembled quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The excitonic structure in quantum dots is studied by polarization-resolved spectroscopy. For symmetric dots magneto-PL measurements show that the spin-relaxation time depends on the splitting of the exciton spin states. At magnetic field spin polarization is conserved within the timescale of exciton recombination.

articleTitle: Light collection properties of integrated fully coated fused-silica SNOM probes
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Hybrid AFM probes, fully aluminum coated, are mounted into a scanning near-field optical microscope and used purely for light collection. Their characteristics in coherent imaging of sub-wavelength structures are investigated both experimentally and theoretically. An experimental spectroscopic response study is also performed.

articleTitle: Selective manipulation of nano-objects using optical forces
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present a scheme to trap and manipulate selectively nano-objects above a dielectric substrate using a near-field apertureless probe.

articleTitle: Visualization of the time dependent nuclear wave-packets in a localized optical center
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The time evolution of the shape of the nuclear wave packet has been directly observed by using 40 fs resolution luminescence spectroscopy in self-trapped excitons in halogen bridged platinum complexes. A 240-step movie was produced.

articleTitle: Coherent optical control of electron spin interaction and dynamics
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A theory of optical control via the virtual excitation of excitons of the spin dynamics of an electron in a single semiconductor quantum dot and of the interaction dynamics of two spins in two neighboring dots is reported. Its relevance to quantum information processing is given. The current status of the relevant experimental development is surveyed.

articleTitle: Indistinguishable photons from a single-photon device
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The quantum-mechanical indistinguishability of consecutive single photons emitted by a quantum dot in a microcavity is tested through a Hong-Ou-Mandel-type two-photon interference experiment. A mean photon wavepacket overlap of 0.81 is inferred from the measurements.

articleTitle: Quantum process tomography with entangled photons
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Using entangled photons from parametric down-conversion as optical qubits, we characterize single- and multiple-qubit operations by quantum process tomography. This allows complete characterization of the operations, including decoherence.

articleTitle: Short-range correlations and field enhancements in cw random laser media
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have experimentally investigated spatial correlations in laser speckle to confirm the presence of short-range structural features consistent with sub-wavelength localization in cw random laser media.

articleTitle: Observation of diffuse terahertz pulse propagation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report the first observation of the diffusive propagation of single-cycle terahertz pulses in a random medium. Coherent detection permits characterization of the statistics of both the amplitude and phase of the random waveform.

articleTitle: A new capability of cascaded quadratic processes: controllable red and blue shift of femtosecond pulses
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We theoretically and experimentally demonstrate the controllable frequency shift of femtosecond pulses in quadratic media in the presence of group velocity mismatch. Applications of this new capability to the compensation of Raman scattering and high-energy pulse compression are discussed.

articleTitle: Generation of two-qubit polarization maximally entangled mixed states
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Using type-I down-conversion, we extend the boundaries of experimentally accessible two-qubit polarization states. Specifically, we create and characterize maximally entangled mixed states that lie above the Werner state boundary in the tangle-entropy plane.

articleTitle: Optical frequency metrology with femtosecond laser pulses
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We explore the possibilities of frequency combs generated by femtosecond lasers in ultra high precision spectroscopy on atomic hydrogen at the 10/sup -14/ level and we have done fundamental tests of the fs frequency comb technique down to the 10/sup -21/ level. Further applications arise in the time domain where now the phase slip between carrier and envelope of such pulses can be controlled.

articleTitle: Controlled collisions with neutral atoms in optical lattices
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: By using state selective optical potentials for neutral atoms stored in an optical lattice potential, we demonstrate controlled collisions between atoms on neighbouring lattice sites. Such a system can be of great use for quantum information processing or for simulating fundamental condensed matter physics Hamiltonians.

articleTitle: Experimental verification of continuous-variable tripartite entanglement
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A continuous-variable tripartite entangled state is experimentally generated by superimposing three independent squeezed vacuum states. We verify the entanglement by measuring the variances of total momentum and relative positions.

articleTitle: Determination of anisotropic dipole moments in single self-assembled quantum dots using Rabi-oscillation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: By investigating the polarization-dependent Rabi oscillations, we determine the respective dipole moments of the two excitonic states |E/sub 1,x/> and |E/sub 1,y/> of a single self-assembled quantum dot that are split due to the shape anisotropy.

articleTitle: Teleportation of a squeezed state
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Continuous variable teleportation of a squeezed state is investigated. We verify that the quantum teleportation process preserves the less variance of a squeezed state than that of a coherent state.

articleTitle: Physics of II-VI microcavities
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Semiconductor microcavities exhibit unusual and exciting optical properties when the strong exciton-photon coupling regime is achieved and yields polaritons. II-VI materials with very robust excitons are particularly well suited to study the physics of 2D-polaritons in microcavities.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optical properties of noble metals at the interband transition threshold
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report measurements of the cubic optical susceptibility of copper at the interband transition threshold. Both real and imaginary parts of the susceptibility are determined from nonlinear transmission and reflection experiments with a copper/silica composite sample irradiated by picosecond laser pulses.

articleTitle: Generation of high-power, non-frequency shifted solitons in a gas-filled photonic band-gap fiber
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We generate femtosecond, non-frequency shifted solitons with peak powers greater than 5 MW in a Xe-filled, hollow-core photonic band-gap fiber. This represents, to our knowledge, the first observation of temporal solitons with no self-frequency shift.

articleTitle: Effects of strain on carrier recombination in GaN quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Strain-induced modification of recombination dynamics in single layer (SQDs) and stacked (MQDs) GaN quantum dots is compared by time-resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy. Large strain induced built-in fields increases the radiative recombination time in SQDs by over an order of magnitude while stacking significantly reduces nonradiative recombination channels and increases the emission efficiency at room temperature.

articleTitle: Femtosecond infrared filaments in air: a source of coherent THz radiation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We observe coherent THz emission from a 1-m plasma string produced by an IR fs laser pulse in atmosphere. The THz pulse is detected perpendicular to the laser propagation axis using heterodyne detection.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a room temperature single-photon laser control of single dye molecule fluorescence in photonic-band-gap cholesteric liquid crystal host
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Operation of a single photon source is demonstrated via photon antibunching in the fluorescence of single terrylene molecules embedded in a cholesteric host. The use of a one-dimensional photonic band gap of planar aligned cholesteric layers will allow further increase in the source efficiency.

articleTitle: Interplay of the spin dynamics of trions and the two-dimensional electron gas in CdTe/Cd/sub 0.85/ Mg/sub 0.15/Te quantum wells
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We have demonstrated that the spin of the electron gas in CdTe quantum wells is polarized via trions formation and its polarization remains even when trions has recombined with a non complete depolarization.

articleTitle: Speckle averaged spectral interferometry of scattering in single and multiple quantum wells
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The resonant light scattering dynamics of multiple GaAs quantum wells measured by speckle averaged spectral interferometry shows a strong and fast initial component not present for single wells which is attributed to radiative coupling.

articleTitle: Experimental observation of modulational instability and spontaneous pattern formation with incoherent "white" light
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report the first observation of modulation instability and spontaneous pattern formation with incoherent "white" light emitted from an incandescent light bulb.

articleTitle: Coherent nonlinear optical response from single GaAs quantum dot trions
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Coherent nonlinear optical measurements on individual charged quantum dots show trion dipole dephasing rates comparable to single excitons with negligible contributions from pure dephasing. The results are a step towards full coherent optical control of single electron spins.

articleTitle: Graphical solution of coherent Raman systems using the Bloch sphere
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present an analysis of coherent Raman systems (e.g. lambda and double lambda systems) based on a Bloch vector representation of the atomic state. The resulting vector equation suggests simple graphical solutions which provide significant intuition regarding the behavior of Raman systems.

articleTitle: Optical orientation of spin polarized holes in bulk GaAs
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Optical orientation of spin-polarized heavy and light holes followed by relaxation to other valence subband states has been observed unambiguously in undoped bulk GaAs. The spin relaxation time for the heavy holes is 110 fs /spl plusmn/ 10%.

articleTitle: Violation of Bell's inequality near 1550 nm using an all-fiber source of polarization-entangled photon pairs
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate a 2 /spl sigma/ violation of a form of Bell's inequality using polarization-entangled photons generated and detected in the 1550 nm telecom band. Polarization-entangled photon pairs are produced by pumping a nonlinear-fiber Sagnac interferometer with orthogonally-polarized pulses.

articleTitle: Experimental and numerical investigation of fundamental noise on supercontinuum generated in microstructure fiber
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Supercontinua generated in microstructure fiber can exhibit amplitude fluctuations of 70%. Experimental and numerical studies of the broadband noise reveal its fundamental and quantum origins: input pulse shot noise and spontaneous Raman scattering.

articleTitle: Second-harmonic generation and reflectance-difference: a meeting of two surface spectroscopies
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Second-harmonic (SH) and reflectance-difference (RD) spectra of vicinal oxidized Si(001) surfaces near the E/sub 1/ resonance reveal similar structure in their lowest-order anisotropic Fourier component, suggesting a common origin in the step-edges.

articleTitle: Non-classical transport regimes of excitons in semiconductor quantum wells
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We monitor directly non-classical transport of quantum-well excitons. The excitons propagate coherently up to four hundreds nanometers, followed by a hot-exciton transport on a length scale of several micrometers at low temperatures.

articleTitle: Hyperfine interactions in a charged quantum dot
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: High-resolution photoluminescence spectroscopy of individual quantum dots charged with single electrons reveals fine structure arising from the Zeeman interaction and hyperfine structure arising from interaction between the electron spin and the underlying nuclear spin.

articleTitle: Many-particle theory of all-optical polarization switching in semiconductor quantum wells
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A microscopic many-body theory is used to analyze an all-optical polarization switching technique that has been demonstrated recently. The respective contributions of phase-space blocking and various exciton interaction and correlation terms to the switching process are calculated.

articleTitle: Exciton-phonon interaction in semiconductors with intermediate polar coupling
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The influence of excitonic effects on dephasing and relaxation processes in semiconductors with intermediate polar coupling is studied. Additional resonances in the optical spectra and strongly enhanced dephasing near the band-edge are discussed.

articleTitle: Single nano-slit and nano-hole spectroscopy in the near and the far-field
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Emission patterns, both in the near and the far-field, are studied on single nano-holes and nano-slits punctured in optically thick metal films. The results suggest that excitation of surface plasmons also plays an important role for light transmission through non-periodic nanostructures.

articleTitle: Quantum logic operations in optical fibers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We have recently demonstrated several probabilistic quantum logic operations using linear optics and post selection. Here we show how the fidelity of these devices can be increased using fibers to reduce optical mode mismatch errors.

articleTitle: Ultrafast conductivity dynamics in pentacene probed using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present measurements of the transient photoconductivity in pentacene single crystals using optical pump THz-probe spectroscopy. The temperature and fluence dependence of both photoinduced mobility and its dynamics are characterized.

articleTitle: Rabi flopping of intersubband transitions in GaAs/AlGaAs MQWs
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Rabi flopping of intersubband transitions in n-type modulation-doped GaAs/AlGaAs multiple quantum wells is directly observed by electro-optic sampling of ultrashort THz transients with large electric-field amplitudes transmitted through the sample.

articleTitle: Collisions of two-dimensional quadratic solitons in type I non-critically phase matched KNbO/sup 3/
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We experimentally investigated planar two soliton collisions in type I non-critically phase matched KNbO/sub 3/. Phase dependent energy exchange processes were shown for nearly collinear beams. A particular case of collided beams showed a three-soliton output.

articleTitle: Terahertz pulse shaping via optical rectification in poled lithium niobate
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate a novel technique for terahertz pulse shaping via optical rectification in the pre-engineered domain structure of poled lithium niobate crystals. The terahertz waveforms map out the corresponding crystal domain structures.

articleTitle: Systematic transmission characterization of 2D InP photonic crystal membrane structures
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Two-dimensional photonic crystal membranes integrated with ridge-waveguides were fabricated in InP/InGaAsP and characterized by optical transmission measurements A photonic band-gap with at least 20 dB extinction was observed. Accurate band-edge tuning by varying r/a is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Electromagnetically-induced transparency at the exciton resonance
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report the experimental demonstration of electromagnetically-induced transparency (EIT) in a GaAs quantum well, in which the absorption of an exciton resonance is reduced by more than twenty-fold. The destructive quantum interference for EIT is set up by a biexciton coherence.

articleTitle: Quantum noise measurements of electron states via phase sensitive detection
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We introduce electron field coherent states that exhibit full coherence. We employ these states in developing a theory of phase-sensitive homodyne detection and measuring the current noise benchmarked against the standard quantum noise limit.

articleTitle: Photoluminescence up-conversion involving surface states in colloidal CdTe quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Efficient photoluminescence up-conversion was observed in colloidal CdTe quantum dots with an energy gain of /spl sim/360 meV. We attribute this up-converted signal to the recombination of carriers from conduction band and hole surface states, respectively.

articleTitle: Terahertz intra-exciton transitions: new views of ultrafast exciton dynamics
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We discuss experiments that resolve the time evolution of exciton populations by sensing transitions between the exciton's internal levels. The dynamical interplay of optically-induced excitons and unbound electron-hole pairs is investigated under various initial conditions.

articleTitle: Demonstration of THz all-optical modulation based on coherent controls
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Using quantum coherent controls we demonstrate THz all-optical modulation in GaAs/AlGaAs quantum wells. This demonstration overcomes population decay-time limited optical switching methods and opens a door to THz all-optical quantum information communications.

articleTitle: Efficient extraction of polarization-entanglement in ultrafast type-II SPDC
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report an entanglement extraction scheme in which polarization-entangled photons are generated in ultrafast type-II SPDC without the need for spectral filters. High-quality polarization entanglement is possible, regardless of pump pulse duration or crystal thickness.

articleTitle: Theory of spatial profiles of exciton and biexciton emission in a single quantum disk
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: This study develops a quantitative theory necessary to estimate the ratio of the FWHM of the spatial distribution of the biexciton emission to the exciton emission patterns and to understand the dependence of that ratio on the quantum disk radius. An interesting feature predicted by the this theory is the spatial distribution of the emission from the excited exciton states. The spatial pattern of the emission intensity shows various features, reflecting the symmetry of the wavefunction of the center-of-mass motion.

articleTitle: Quantum interference injection and control of spin-polarized transient current gratings in GaAs
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Transient grating and quantum interference techniques are combined to inject and control spin-polarized currents (with or without an accompanying electrical current) in bulk GaAs at room temperature.

articleTitle: Efficient single-mode generation of degenerate 1550 nm entanglement in type-II parametric downconversion
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. The first experiment on a source based on type-II parametric downconversion for beam-like creation of a pair of degenerate, entangled photons at 1550 nm produced in a 12 mm long BBO crystal is reported. The crystal is pumped with a femtosecond pulsed Ti-sapphire laser operating at 775 nm. The coupling is optimized by focusing the pump so that the crystal emits each pair of photons into a mode which has a maximum possible overlap-integral with the collection mode of the single-mode fiber. Calculations of the single-mode emission efficiency are performed considering beamsize and wavevector spread for a long crystal with strong focusing. With this optimization we experimentally get high singles-rates even with the relatively poor performance of the single photon detectors available at near-infrared.

articleTitle: Subpicosecond luminescence spectroscopy of hot carrier dynamics in homoepitaxial GaN
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Femtosecond UV luminescence downconversion is used to study hot carrier relaxation in homoepitaxial GaN through measurement of PL rise times for varying carrier excitation energies and densities.

articleTitle: Doubly phase-matched cascaded wave mixing in tapered fibers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Doubly phase-matched cascaded four-wave mixing in tapered fibers is demonstrated using femtosecond Cr:forsterite laser pulses. The first stage of this cascade involves phase-matched third-harmonic generation. At the second stage, the third harmonic and fundamental radiation generate new spectral components through phase-matched parametric wave mixing.

articleTitle: Phase inversion of second-harmonic generation from Si(001) surfaces
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The azimuthal phase of second-harmonic generation from Si(001) surfaces exhibits inversion as a function of photon energy or interface chemical bond for the correct polarization configurations, providing information on resonances or bond polarity.

articleTitle: Improved coherent THz emission by modification of the dielectric environment
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate that by modifying the dielectric environment the internal conversion efficiency of a coherent THz surface field emitter is significantly improved.

articleTitle: Clean and scalable quantum logic with trapped ions
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Experimental progress in constructing a quantum computer with a collection of trapped ions is discussed, with emphasis on how various technical hurdles may be circumvented.

articleTitle: Near-field spectroscopy of InAs single quantum dots at 70 K
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate high-resolution near-field optical microscopy of self-assembled single semiconducting InAs/GaAs QDs at liquid nitrogen temperature of 70 K. We have reduced the number of excited QDs as well as the background photoluminescence (PL) from the barrier layer by simultaneously employing both shadow mask apertures produced by 100 run dielectric microspheres and a 30 (or 100) run apertured fiber probe that allow enhanced spatial and optical resolution at 70 K.

articleTitle: Femtosecond pulse breakup and compression in resonant multiple quantum wells
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We study the propagation of subpicosecond pulses resonant to the hhl's exciton in Bragg-periodic and detuned multiple quantum wells. We show pulse breakup depending on the radiative interwell coupling, excitation-induced dephasing and nonlinear pulse compression.

articleTitle: Geometry dependence of Auger carrier capture rates into self-assembled quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present calculations of Auger carrier capture processes into self-assembled quantum dots. A strong dependence of the Auger capture rate on the size and geometry of the quantum dots is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Cavity pattern formation and cavity solitons with incoherent light
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We show that patterns and solitons can form when spatially and temporally incoherent light circulates in a passive nonlinear cavity with noninstantaneous medium. The pattern formation process is always associated with two consecutive thresholds. The first (instability) threshold is unaffected by the cavity boundary conditions, whereas the second threshold is induced by the feedback through the interplay of nonlinear gain and cavity loss.

articleTitle: Radiative decay and dephasing in plasmonic band gap structures
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report spatial and spectral domain measurements of the dephasing of surface plasmon excitations in metal films with periodic nano-hole arrays. A Rayleigh-like scattering of surface plasmons by the periodic hole array is the microscopic origin of the dephasing.

articleTitle: Discrete Ginzburg-Landau solitons in laser arrays
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate that discrete solitons are possible in laser arrays described by Ginzburg-Landau lattices. As a result of discreteness, we find that this system exhibits novel features that have no counterpart whatsoever in either the continuous limit or in other conservative discrete models.

articleTitle: Resonant emission and transmission of infrared radiation by microstructured surfaces supporting surface phonon-polaritons
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A new phenomenon has been demonstrated recently dealing with radiative properties of microstructured surfaces. It has been shown that light can be resonantly transmitted by a film with a periodic array of holes due to the excitation of surface plasmons. In this paper, we report similar results in the infrared due to the excitation of surface phonon-polaritons. Another striking property of microstructured surfaces supporting surface phonon-polaritons is their ability to emit light in very narrow solid angles. In this paper, we show that it is also possible to design a surface that allows to emit light isotropically with a 100% emissivity. Experimental results are reported.

articleTitle: Measurements of the orbital geometric phase
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper presents measurements of the orbital geometric phase by interferometric technique. This study focuses on the phases and spaces of first and second order modes. These modes are expressed in terms of Hermite-Gauss and Laguerre-Gauss functions. For the case of transformations between first order modes the path could be followed geometrically on the orbital Poincare sphere. For all paths investigated in first and second order spaces the measurements of the magnitude and sign of the geometric phase are in excellent agreement with the theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Ultrafast dephasing and collective effects in strongly correlated systems
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Using a recent theory of the ultrafast nonlinear optical response of strongly correlated systems, I will show that correlations governed by the dynamics of the magnetoplasmon (MP) excitations dominate the four-wave-mixing (FWM) spectrum of the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) in the quantum Hall effect (QHE) regime.

articleTitle: Ultrafast near-field spectroscopy of correlated exciton states in single quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present the first femtosecond study of the coherent nonlinear optical response of single and correlated excitonic levels in single quantum dots. We find an enhanced dephasing rate of the biexcitonic polarization.

articleTitle: Band offsets measurement of Si-SiO/sub 2/ interfaces by internal photoemission induced second-harmonic generation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We measured the Si valence to SiO/sub 2/ conduction band offset via multiphoton internal-photoemission induced second-harmonic generation for the first time, providing a noninvasive sensitive tool for band offsets measurement in wide variety of semiconductor interfaces.

articleTitle: Exciton spin coherence via Coulomb correlations
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report experimental studies of exciton spin coherence induced via correlations between excitons with opposite spins, including correlations associated with two-exciton scattering states. Electromagnetically-induced transparency is used to probe the spin coherence.

articleTitle: Sub-femtosecond resolution wave packet measurements using correlated pairs
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Correlation offers a new route to time resolved measurements. Exploiting correlation we measure H/sub 2//sup +/ double ionization dynamics with sub-femtosecond precision and we measure vibrational wave packet dynamics in D/sub 2//sup +/ with ∼0.03- Angstrom, ∼200-Attosecond precision.

articleTitle: Excited state relaxation dynamics of novel boron-nitrogen-bridged charge transfer organometallic compounds
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We employ two-color ultrafast spectroscopy to investigate the picosecond relaxation dynamics of the metal-to-ligand charge transfer in a class of novel organometallic compounds incorporating boron-nitrogen bridges between donor and multiple organic acceptor ligands.

articleTitle: Impulsive stimulated Raman scattering of molecular vibrations using nonlinear pulse shaping
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate the excitation of a molecular vibrational coherence via impulsive stimulated Raman scattering using a pump pulse longer than the vibrational period of the excited mode.

articleTitle: Polarization and power scaling of harmonics from solid and targets in the /spl lambda//sup 3/-regime
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Harmonic generation mechanisms are studied in the ultrafast (22 fs), relativistic regime (I/spl lambda//sup 2//spl sim/10/sup 18/ W/cm/sup 2/). Analysis of the polarization and intensity dependence of the harmonics illustrates different mechanisms of harmonic production for odd and even harmonics.

articleTitle: Quantum algorithms in the presence of decoherence: optical experiments
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We demonstrate the application of linear optical interferometers to performing quantum algorithms. In particular, we show how the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm can be implemented in the presence of noise by using decoherence-free subspaces.

articleTitle: Generation and propagation of coherent THz folded acoustic phonons
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report on the propagation of coherent folded acoustic phonons with frequencies near 1 THz. The folded phonons are generated with femtosecond optical pulses and detected, with little attenuation, after traversing 1.2 /spl mu/m of bulk GaAs.

articleTitle: A new type of optical manipulation of nanoscale objects
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We theoretically investigate the radiation forces on nanoscale objects confining excitons. A new type of optical manipulation utilizing the quantum mechanical properties of the individual objects can be realized by using the resonant light.

articleTitle: Tunable optical excitations in gold nanorings
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The optical response of gold nanorings is measured and analyzed theoretically. Compared to gold disks, nanorings exhibit a red-shifted surface plasmon that can be tuned by varying the ratio between ring thickness arid radius.

articleTitle: Limitations on the measurement of spatial coherence by near-field probes
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Using a scalar dipole model, we find that the fundamental limitation on the measurement of spatial coherence by near-field probes can be understood in terms of a simple scattering model.

articleTitle: Optical generation of many-spin entangled states in a quantum well
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A novel method is proposed to generate spin entangled states in a semiconductor quantum well using ultrafast laser pulses. Time-domain differential reflectivity measurements reveal entangled states involving at least three non-interacting q-bits.

articleTitle: Aerodynamic window: novel diagnostic tool to characterize filaments
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present a novel technique that allows direct measurement of filament properties such as beam size, energy, and spectrum by using an aerowindow.

articleTitle: Photon-pairs generation in micro-structured fiber
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate correlated photon-pair generation using four-wave mixing in micro-structured fiber. The anomalous group dispersion just above the zero-dispersion point ensures phase-matching. We obtained coincidence-counting rate significantly over the accidental counting rate.

articleTitle: Optical spectroscopy and control of single defect centers in solids
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The nitrogen-vacancy defect center in diamond is characterized by a weak coupling to the environment plus a electron spin paramagnetic ground and optically excited state. One thus can manipulate and read single spin states in these defect centers. Another type of defect can be ionized in a controlled way which may provide a means for future high density data storage on a single defect center level.

articleTitle: Attosecond metrology
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Recent advances in the generation of attosecond-duration electromagnetic pulses demand the development of methods to measure them. The combination of sources and measurement technology provides an important set of tools for the study of electron dynamics in matter of all kinds, I survey several recent proposals for attoseconds metrology, and compare their efficacy and range of applicability.

articleTitle: Plasmonic left-handed materials in optics
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Left-handed materials with negative refraction in the optical range are proposed based on metal nanowire structures. The optical properties of such nanocomposites and their novel applications are also discussed.

articleTitle: Optoelectronic control of electron and nuclear spins in semiconductor nanostructures
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper presents an overview of recent developments in coherent electronic and spin dynamics in semiconductors and quantum structures, including a discussion of temporally- and spatially-resolved magneto-optical measurements that reveal an interesting interplay between electronic and nuclear spins. An electrical scheme for local spin manipulation based on g-tensor modulation response (g-TMR) is also presented. The experiments investigate electronic, photonic, and magnetic manipulation of electron and nuclear spins in a variety of semiconductor structures and focus on investigating the underlying physics for quantum information processing in solid state.

articleTitle: Phase stabilization of modelocked lasers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The combination of time and frequency domain techniques has enabled the phase stabilization of modelocked lasers, which has impacted optical frequency metrology and phase sensitive time domain experiments.

articleTitle: Influence of metal frequency dispersion on the properties meta-materials with negative refractive index
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: An analysis of the influence of the metal frequency dispersion on the properties of metamaterials with negative refractive index is presented. Starting from the transmission-reflection coefficients, the effective permittivity, permeability and refractive index is determined.

articleTitle: Infinite order exciton Bloch equations for DFWM
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present a new exciton-based formalism for calculating the coherent response of asymmetric semiconductor multiple quantum well structures to ultra-short optical pulses valid to infinite order in the optical field.

articleTitle: Ultrafast carrier trapping in amorphous semiconductors studied by time-resolved THz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present studies of the ultrafast carrier response in amorphous silicon (a-Si:H) and related materials using time-resolved THz techniques. We find that the initial carrier processes are consistent with trapping on a picosecond time scale.

articleTitle: Observation of spin squeezing in MnF/sub 2/
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate squeezing of the lattice magnetization in antiferromagnetic MnF/sub 2/. Our method uses femtosecond optical pulses to create coherences involving magnon pairs.

articleTitle: Sub-diffraction-limit imaging based on the topographic contrast of differential confocal microscopy
