publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Using the nanometer topographic sensitivity of differential confocal microscopy, we detect surface features with lateral dimensions smaller than the diffraction limit without fluorescence labeling. Lateral resolution as high as 0.2/spl lambda/ is achieved with maximum-likelihood image restoration.

articleTitle: The asymmetric transmission properties of a single dressed sub-wavelength aperture
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate that the optical transmission properties of a sub-wavelength aperture with surrounding periodic nanostructuring are determined primarily by the properties of the illuminated surface. This is in sharp contrast to the behavior of a periodic array of sub-wavelength apertures.

articleTitle: Nanophotonic switching using CuCl quantum cubes
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report the first demonstration of repeated near-field optical switching using cubic CuCl quantum dots by time-resolved optical near-field measurement. Its figure of merit is 10-100 times greater than that of conventional photonic switches.

articleTitle: Separability criterion for separate quantum systems
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We develop a sufficiency criterion for quantum separability, valid for arbitrary states of two arbitrary systems. Our criterion confirms spin entanglement of two macroscopic atomic samples in experiments by Julsgaard, Kozhekin, and Polzik [Nature (2001)].

articleTitle: Atomic vapor-based high efficiency photon detectors
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We describe a detector for weak optical fields employing an atomic vapor as the active medium, combined with the "cycling transition" readout perfected for ion traps. Theoretical calculations suggest detection efficiency >99% may be attainable.

articleTitle: Control of multiphoton excitation in condensed phases based on multiphoton intrapulse interference
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Phase-modulated ultrafast pulses are used to control nonlinear optical processes in large organic molecules and solids. The principle of multiphoton intrapulse interference is used to predict the required phase to enhance or suppress the process.

articleTitle: Solid-state random lasers: small size, broad variety
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The paper reviews the history and the state of the art of random lasers, simplest miniature sources of stimulated emission without cavity.

articleTitle: White light solitons
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present numerical analysis of white-light solitons in noninstantaneous nonlinear media, and lay down general requirements for soliton formation.

articleTitle: Luminescence quenching in a random medium
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have investigated the origin of quenching of visible photoluminescence in Yb,Er:yttria nanopowders. We show that this phenomenon results from a thermal nonlinearity mediated by non-radiative processes at high temperatures, using the results of luminescence decay measurements together with a simple theoretical model.

articleTitle: Theory and experiment of a short-pulse-laser pumped distributed feedback optical parametric oscillator
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have developed the theory of a distributed-feedback optical-parametric oscillator pumped by a laser pulse length shorter than the round-trip length of the nonlinear gain material. We also demonstrated distributed-feedback optical-parametric oscillation in a 5-cm PPLN crystal pumped by a 430-ps passively Q-switched Nd:YAG laser.

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband phase matching of optical frequency conversion using transient molecular birefringence
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We show that transient birefringence imposed in a molecular gas with a femtosecond laser pulse phase matches nonlinear frequency conversion-with bandwidths that support 1 fs laser pulses with up to a 20% conversion efficiency.

articleTitle: Breaking diffraction limit with meta-materials
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Pendry's superlens has been verified in microwave optics analog with meta-materials. Simulation with finite-element solver of Maxwell equations is further used to explore the feature. Aberration-like issues are also discussed.

articleTitle: An experimental investigation of criteria for continuous variable entanglement
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Motivated by previous observations on the characterization of entangled optical beams, this paper presents a characterization of entanglement not only in terms of inseparability, but also by its mixedness. The entanglement is presented on a diagram of the average sideband photon number required to generate the entanglement (a property synonymous to inseparability) versus the average number of excess sideband photons, as deduced from the measured values of the quadrature variances. The efficacy contours of some common quantum information protocols are also displayed.

articleTitle: Precise timing stabilization of a mode-locked laser at 1550 nm to an optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Using high-bandwidth feedback, we have synchronized the pulse train from a mode-locked semiconductor laser to an optical clock and achieved the lowest timing jitter (20 fs, 10 Hz to 10 MHz) for such devices.

articleTitle: Stability of a strongly-attractive, two-component Fermi gas
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Using a simple model, we show that a strongly-attractive, two-component Fermi gas of atoms should be mechanically stable as a consequence of unitarity. We demonstrate this stability experimentally in a degenerate gas of /sup 6/Li atoms.

articleTitle: Phase and intensity dependence of the dynamical Franz-Keldysh effect
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We model theoretically the dependence of excitonic absorption spectra of semiconductor quantum wells in intense THz electric fields on the phase and intensity of those fields, and discuss the implications of our results for experiment.

articleTitle: High-fidelity quantum logic operations and entangled ancilla states
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We describe a high-fidelity approach to linear optics quantum computing in which the quantum logic operations always produce an output. A method for generating the required entangled states is also described.

articleTitle: Spin in semimagnetic CdMnTe quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The optical properties of magnetic quantum dots are studied. Micro-photoluminescence spectroscopy reveals that single dot emission lines are broadened due to magnetic moment fluctuations. Polarization resolved measurements show that even at zero field emission from CdMnTe quantum dots is strongly circularly polarized.

articleTitle: Intrinsic optical bistability of black body radiation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report experimental observations of optically-induced bistable switching of black body radiation emitted by a random medium.

articleTitle: Femtosecond laser-induced nanofabrication in the near field of an atomic force microscope tip
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Femtosecond laser-induced formation of nanostructures in the near field of an atomic force microscope tip is demonstrated. Mechanism of nanofabrication will be discussed.

articleTitle: Design of near-field optical nanostructures for enhanced second-harmonic generation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present optical nanostructure designs for enhancement of second harmonic generation based on near-field localization and phase matching effects, and analyze these nanostructures using a rigorous electromagnetic modeling tool.

articleTitle: Direct observation of optically injected spin-polarized currents in semiconductors
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Direct experimental evidence for the spin-polarization of optically injected ballistic spin currents by coherent one and two photon excitation in unbiased semiconductors is provided via the detection of a phase-dependent movement of the circularly polarized photoluminescence in ZnSe.

articleTitle: Qubit rotation with multiple phase-locked pulses in single quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Coherent optical control of qubits in single quantum dots shows that rotation of a single qubit can be achieved with multiple phase-locked pulses. Two pulses with well-defined pulse areas (/spl sim//spl pi//2) are phase-adjusted to rotate the qubit between |0> and |1>.

articleTitle: Dispersion-cancelled tomographic measurements using entangled photons
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: This study presents the first experimental demonstration of quantum optical coherence tomography (QOCT) technique using a thin window of glass as a sample. The dispersion cancellation capability is exhibited by carrying out the measurement on the same sample after burying it under a highly dispersive medium. A detailed comparison of these results are also presented with measurements performed by classical OCT.

articleTitle: Triggered single-photon and photon-pair emission from acceptor bound excitons in a semiconductor
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate the generation of triggered single photons at a predetermined and well defined energy and two-photon emission with slightly different emission energies using the radiative recombination of individual nitrogen-bound excitons in ZnSe:N.

articleTitle: Direct measurement of spatial coherence of light in Wigner representation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We demonstrate experimentally a novel technique for characterizing transverse spatial coherence using the Wigner function, based on area-integrated detection of interference between a pair of rotated and displaced replicas of the input beam.

articleTitle: Current-induced anisotropy in the susceptibility of a free electron gas
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present experimental data for current-induced anisotropy in the susceptibility of a two-dimensional electron gas. This novel effect is in principle independent of extrinsic properties of the semiconductor and occurs solely due to a shift in the steady-state distribution function of the electron gas.

articleTitle: Out of this world: The future of atomic clocks
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. The development of future atomic clocks at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is discussed. The atomic fountain clock called NIST-F1, the primary frequency standard at NIST, is designed to measure the energy splitting of the hyperfine ground states of the /sup 133/Cs atom with a very high degree of accuracy. The next generation of fountain clock is currently being designed at NIST and is in the early stages of testing. One modification to the apparatus will be to cool the drift region to cryogenic temperature, thereby reducing the correction for the black-body radiation frequency shift to a negligible level. An additional modification will be to reduce the atom density during the measurement while increasing the atom throughput in order to reduce the cold-collision frequency shift. Another up-and-coming frequency standard in progress is the Primary Atomic Reference Clock in Space (PARCS) project, which is an atomic-clock mission currently scheduled to fly aboard the International Space Station (ISS) in 2007. The mission involves a laser-cooled cesium atomic clock and a time-transfer system using the Global Positioning System satellites. The microgravity environment aboard the ISS will allow for observation times much longer than feasible on earth. The objectives of the mission are to test gravitational theory and to realize the second with an uncertainty of 1×10/sup -16/ - a factor of 10 better than that achieved on earth.

articleTitle: Observation of large "fast light" pulse advancement without distortion
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We observe pulses advanced by 15% of their width and experiencing only minor distortion using laser-driven potassium atoms in a novel configuration that avoids competing nonlinear optical effects.

articleTitle: Precise phase control of short pulses
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We will discuss the strong impact of precision phase control of optical pulses to fields ranging from ultrafast science Io precision metrology.

articleTitle: Directed diffusion in a symmetric optical lattice
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We report the observation of directed diffusion in a symmetric periodic potential. This has been realized with cold atoms in a one-dimensional dissipative optical lattice. A zero mean force temporary asymmetric induces the directed motion of a Brownian particle.

articleTitle: Polarization effect in impulsive rotational Raman scattering in a hydrogen gas
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We theoretically show that an elliptically polarized fs pulse impulsively excites rotational Raman coherence in a hydrogen gas more efficiently than a linearly polarized pulse. The phonon amplitude dramatically depends on ellipticity and propagation distance.

articleTitle: Use of Rb transitions to lock both the wavelength and repetition rate of a mode-locked laser
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The fluorescence and index of refraction of two-photon resonant rubidium are investigated as a function of repetition rate and wavelength of a mode-locked train of pulses.

articleTitle: Influence of non-radiative transfer on the ultrafast electron dynamics of metallic nanoparticles
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Ultrafast dynamics of electron relaxation in a nanometallic particle has been the subject of many studies in the past ten years. New and partially unexplained behaviours have been observed experimentally by different groups. In this paper we show that by introducing a decay channel not taken into account so far, it is possible to interpret the size and fluence dependence of the decay time observed experimentally.

articleTitle: Magnetization-induced second-harmonic generation magneto-photonic microcavity
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The nonlinear magneto-optical Kerr effect in second-harmonic generation in yttrium-iron garnet magneto-photonic microcavity is studied. The strong magnetization-induced variations in second-harmonic intensity and polarization plane rotation are observed.

articleTitle: Fabrication of hyperboloid-drum structures for sub micro- to nano-meter sized emitters
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report characteristics of newly devised hyperboloid-drum structures to reduce the active layer diameter to sub micro-meter while maintaining the wide area for easy electrode connection. The active layer diameters, the etched-waist of /spl sim/ 8 /spl mu/m-tall hyperboloid-drum, can be adjusted down to /spl sim/ 100 nm.

articleTitle: Higher order waveguide modes and cladding aperiodicity effects in hollow photonic-crystal fibers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Higher order waveguide modes of hollow-core photonic-crystal fibers are studied experimentally and theoretically. Cladding aperiodicity is shown to modify the spectrum of modes guided in the hollow core of such fibers, with regions of low-loss guiding still observed as isolated peaks in transmission spectra.

articleTitle: Excitonic signatures in photoluminescence and terahertz absorption
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: By measuring THz absorption and time-resolved photoluminescence on the same GaAs quantum well sample we confirm the recent prediction of Kira that PL at the exciton frequency does not require a population of bound excitons.

articleTitle: Single-qubit, entanglement-assisted and ancilla-assisted quantum process tomography
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Quantum process tomography allows complete and precise characterization of a quantum operation. We report quantum process tomography of unitary, decohering, and partially polarizing operations using single-qubit, maximally entangled, and non-entangled input states.

articleTitle: Toward cavity-QED strong coupling of a semiconductor quantum dot to an external optical micro-cavity
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A hemispherical cavity containing interface-fluctuation GaAs quantum dots was constructed to achieve cavity-QED strong coupling between a cavity mode and a single QD. It consists of a 50-micron radius-of-curvature mirror and a semiconductor DBR mirror.

articleTitle: Terahertz electrooptic modulation of a single biased GaAs quantum well
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We investigate the optical interband properties of GaAs quantum wells driven by a terahertz field. The application of this field shifts the exciton absorption energy. Additionally, terahertz optical sidebands are observed up to 140 K.

articleTitle: Observation of molecular dissociation along several exit channels with parametric four-wave mixing
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Multichannel dissociation of electronically-excited Rb/sub 2/ has been observed with an atomic wavepacket which serves as a sensitive detector. We identify several exit channels through analysis of the amplitude and phase of radiation produced by four-wave-mixing.

articleTitle: Quantum interference control of a ballistic pure spin current in GaAs/AIGaAs quantum wells
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate optical injection of a spin current with no accompanying charge current in GaAs/AlGaAs quantum wells through quantum interference of one- and two-photon absorption of -100 fs phase-locked pulses with orthogonal linear polarizations.

articleTitle: Precision metrology and interferometry with ultracold calcium atoms
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Advances in laser cooling of alkaline earth atoms have reduced trapped atom temperatures from the millikelvin to the microkelvin regime. Using such atoms, our optical atomic clock should have a fractional frequency uncertainty approaching 1 /spl times/ 10/sup -15/. Sub-recoil cooling and two-pulse atom interferometry are also discussed.

articleTitle: Semiconductor laser with delayed incoherent feedback: experimental and numerical studies
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The bifurcation sequence of a semiconductor laser subject to delayed incoherent feedback is studied experimentally and numerically with good agreement. The sequence follows a three frequency scenario beginning with either subcritical or supercritical Hopf bifurcations.

articleTitle: Coulomb and carrier dynamics of 1.3 /spl mu/m quantum dots in tunable two-color pump-probe experiments
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report Coulomb renormalization and carrier thermal activation dynamics in self-assembled quantum dots following selective optical excitation in the ground state using a novel two-color pump-probe technique based on soliton self-frequency shift in microstructure fibers.

articleTitle: Cavity enhanced single and entangled photons from a quantum dot
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We demonstrate a single-photon source based on a quantum dot in a micropost microcavity that exhibits a large Purcell factor (F/sub p/=5) together with a small multi-photon probability (g/sup (2)/(0)=2%). Emitted single photons are nearly Fourier-transform-limited. An extension of this technique can be used to generate entangled photon pairs on demand.

articleTitle: Angle- and spectrally-resolved Bragg scattering on two-dimensional silicon-based photonic crystals
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The angle dependent diffraction efficiency of 2D photonic crystals is measured to be lower than 5/spl middot/10-4 for certain frequencies and unity spectrally nearby in good agreement with numerical calculations, whereby the surface termination is crucial.

articleTitle: Direct multiphoton excitation of molecular ions produces selectively excited fragments
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Strong field induced vacuum ultraviolet fluorescence in argon and molecular nitrogen reveals many excitation processes. Intriguingly, direct laser excitation is exclusive to molecules and selectively produces excited ion fragments with 2s holes.

articleTitle: Bidirectional ring laser as a scatterometer
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present a bidirectional pulsed ring laser working as differential spectrometer to measure absolute scattering coefficient. The threshold for locking the beat note is used and a scattering amplitude, R, of 10/sup -12/ was measured.

articleTitle: Physical mechanism for apparent superluminality in barrier tunneling
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. The apparent superluminal tunneling of wavepackets through photonic bandgaps and other barriers is shown to be a quasi-static process in which the envelope of the input pulse modulates the amplitude of a standing wave.

articleTitle: Laser oscillation with photonic molecule modes in resonantly coupled micro-spheres
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Mode profile and lasing characteristics of resonantly coupled whispering gallery modes of size-matched dye doped polymer spheres placed on semiconductor V-groove are examined. Photonic molecule like behavior is clearly observed.

articleTitle: Stable spatial autosolitons in semiconductor amplifiers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report the first experimental observation of spatial dissipative solitons (autosoliton) in a patterned electrode semiconductor amplifier (SOA). Our results fit with the numerical simulations which support the bifurcating behavior of solitons with current pumping.

articleTitle: Probing adsorbate oscillation on metal surfaces using ultrafast extreme ultraviolet pulses
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We observe the oscillation of CO on a Pt (111) surface excited by ultrafast infrared pulses using time-resolved extreme ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Spontaneous decay trapping and steering in a two-dimensional photonic crystal
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We show that both the spontaneous decay and pulse amplification in near-resonance Bragg structures can produce light localization in the bandgap of such structures. This localization is accompanied by formation of a new type of gap soliton.

articleTitle: Quantum nanoplasmonics: surface plasmon amplification by stimulated emission of radiation (SPASER)
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We make a step towards quantum nanoplasmonics: surface plasmon fields of a nanosystem are quantized and their stimulated emission is considered. We introduce SPASER, a quantum generator for surface plasmon quanta. Spaser is predicted to generate ultrafast (10 to 100 fs duration), temporally coherent, near-atomic intensity fields of surface plasmon modes that are strongly localized on the nanoscale. Those include dark modes that may constitute a basis for background-free enhanced nano-optical spectroscopy. Applications and related phenomena are discussed.

articleTitle: Pulse contrast enhancement of ultra-high-power femtosecond laser pulses
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We determine the conditions under which desirable nonlinear processes such as nonlinear ellipse rotation can be exploited in bulk media at powers that are many times above critical power of self-focusing. Application of this scheme to pulse-contrast enhancement of ultra-high-power laser pulses is explored.

articleTitle: Quantum dot lasing in the strong coupling regime in semiconductor microcavities
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. The coexistence of low threshold lasing in the strong coupling (SC) regime in a high-quality semiconductor microcavity under quasi-resonant optical pumping is reported. In this study, a clear evidence of the simultaneous presence of the perturbative and non-perturbative regimes under the same optical excitation in semiconductor microcavities is observed. An unambiguous anti-crossing behavior of the coupled bare cavity and exciton modes, characteristic of the strong-coupling regime is obtained. Between these eigenstates of the system a new strong line appears whose intensity is exponentially dependent on the pumping power. An intermediate regime in semiconductor microcavities is identified, where this unexpected lasing mode, which fulfills the characteristics of the weak coupling mode, coexists with the free polariton modes. It is shown that this extra mode results from the population inversion of highly localized exciton states that behave as quantum-dot-like trap in the plane of the quantum well. Thus, simultaneous operation of a VCSEL and strongly coupled exciton-polaritons in a cavity is achieved.

articleTitle: Nano-acoustic waveform synthesis and second harmonic generation of coherent acoustic phonon oscillations using optical coherent control
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Second harmonic coherent acoustic phonon oscillations were generated in strained InGaN/GaN multiple quantum wells using an optical coherent control technique. This demonstration leads to the nano acoustic waveform synthesis based on optical coherent controls.

articleTitle: Filamentation in air with twin femtosecond laser pulses
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We study filamentation in air using a sequence of two intense IR femtosecond laser pulses with variable delay. Increased filament length and pulse shortening is observed, in agreement with simulations.

articleTitle: Theory of ultrafast nonlinear refraction in semiconductor heterostructure waveguides
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Considering the symmetry of the third-order susceptibility tensor elements for semiconductor heterostructures results in 8 independent elements for [001] growth. Nonlinear refraction coefficients are derived and the change in dimensionality with intermixing is discussed.

articleTitle: Cold Rydberg gas dynamics and the trapping of cold Rydberg atoms
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We study n- and l-mixing dynamics of cold Rydberg atom gases at varying background radiation temperature and Rydberg atom density in a cryogenic magneto-optical trap.

articleTitle: Multiple re-focusing of ultrashort laser pulse propagating in condensed matter
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We focused a 38 fs laser pulse, which is spatially filtered, into a glass cell containing a very dilute solution of coumarin 440 in methanol. Via three photons fluorescence of coumarin, up to 6 re-focusing filaments were observed along one straight line. This is the first evidence showing a way to control multiple filamentation.

articleTitle: Relaxation and dephasing of multiexcitons in electrically-pumped quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The population relaxation and dephasing of multiexcitonic transitions in InGaAs quantum dots embedded in the active region of an electrically-pumped semiconductor optical amplifier are measured in the temperature range from 10 K to 300 K.

articleTitle: Calculation of photon density dynamics in random lasers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The dynamics of stimulated emission in random laser is calculated in the model of one-dimensional scattering medium with gain, using the rate equations for density of emitted photon and population inversion.

articleTitle: Superluminal reflection from photonic bandgap quarter wave dielectric mirror
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A recently derived analytic equation for the reflection phase from a quarter wave dielectric stack demonstrates a regime of negative mirror penetration depth. Practical geometries are predicted with reasonable reflectivities and measurable superluminal photonic bandgap performance.

articleTitle: Towards far-field fluorescence nanoscopy
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Far-field microscopy has been plagued by the diffraction resolution limit. This is particularly restraining in the case of fluorescence imaging of biological specimens such as live cells. Here we report on the creation spots of excited molecules at the tens of nanometer scale, with focused red light and conventionally focusing optics. The underlying strategy is the engineering of the microscope's point-spread-function by stimulated emission depletion and interference. Sub-diffraction spots enable for the first time far-field fluorescence microscopy with axial resolution at the scale of 30-50 nm.

articleTitle: 420 MHz Cr:forsterite femtosecond ring laser and its use for continuum generation in the 1-2 micron range
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present a Cr:forsterite ring laser producing 30 fs pulses at a 420 MHz repetition rate. The output is broadened in highly nonlinear fiber yielding spectra covering 1050-2200 nm.

articleTitle: Singular optics with polychromatic light: spectral anomalies in diffraction
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We show that spectacular spectral changes take place in the vicinity of the dark rings of the Airy pattern formed with spatially coherent, polychromatic light diffracted at a circular aperture.

articleTitle: Electromagnetically induced absorption and transparency in a single Raman spectrum
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report, observation of both electromagnetically induced absorption (ElA) and electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in sodium vapor in a single Raman spectrum. The sign of the of the coherent feature depends on whether the single-photon detuning favors four-wave mixing or coherent population trapping.

articleTitle: Ultrafast photoinduced softening in a ferromagnetic semiconductor
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Two-color time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr spectroscopy is used to manipulate and detect the dynamics of carrier-induced ferromagnetism in III-V ferromagnetic semiconductors. Our data demonstrates that magnetic properties, e.g., the coercivity, can be tuned reversibly and nonthermally on subpicosecond time scale.

articleTitle: Cavity QED with a continuous cold atom Rb source
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We study field fluctuations from an N atom cavity QED system with low N and have developed a cold Rb beam to lengthen the interaction time of the atoms.

articleTitle: Spatial correlations in time-resolved terahertz speckle patterns
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We describe observations of the angular correlations in speckle patterns formed by a terahertz pulse propagating in a random medium. We obtain a direct measurement of spatial coherence from time- and angle-resolved measurements.

articleTitle: Simultaneous measurement of coherence length and time of quantum-well excitons
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate an efficient method to simultaneously measure both, the coherence length and time, of quantum-well excitons based on photoluminescence with high spatial and temporal resolution.

articleTitle: Collinear optical weak measurements with photonic crystals
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present a theoretical and experimental study of a photonic crystal based optical system in terms of weak values that map polarization states onto longitudinal spatial position and show fast and slow light behavior.

articleTitle: Direct measurement of plasma evolution during supercontinuum generation in a solid
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We have performed, to our knowledge, the first direct measurement of plasma growth during the process of supercontinuum generation in a bulk material. We describe experimental and numerical results for sapphire and fused silica.

articleTitle: The carrier-wave Mollow triplet in experiments on GaAs excited by 5 fs pulses
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: With intense 5 fs pulses and improved sample design, we observe the carrier-wave Mollow triplet in bulk GaAs. A dependence on the carrier-envelope offset phase is expected.

articleTitle: Delay-time dependent adatom desorption from the Si(111)-7/spl times/7 surface using femtosecond optical pulse pair excitation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Using femtosecond pulse-pair excitation at 800-nm, delay-time dependent adatom desorption from the Si(111)-7/spl times/7 surface was observed by scanning tunneling microscopy. Trends in the desorption yield and site selectivity were detected as a function of delay time.

articleTitle: Optical manipulation of liposomes and hydrosomes
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We have demonstrated the optical trapping and induced fusion of liposomes and hydrosomes (stable water droplets) as containers for controlled chemical reactions with ultra-small volumes.

articleTitle: Optical read-out and initialization of an electron spin in a single quantum dot
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have shown theoretically that the read-out of a single electron spin is viable through resonant excitation of a trion with circularly polarized light, and suggest a feasible protocol for the spin initialization.

articleTitle: Discrete quadratic solitons in waveguide arrays
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Quadratic soliton formation in an array of coupled PPLN channel waveguides was experimentally demonstrated for the first time. The discrete features of the solitons predicted by theory were observed.

articleTitle: Multiexcitons squeezed into the sub-excitonic volume of a colloidal quantum dot
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Spectroscopic and dynamical measurements of multiexciton states in CdSe colloidal quantum dots (QDs) reveal room-temperature stable biexcitons and triexcitons. Strong spatial confinement in "ultrasmall" colloidal QDs results in enhanced multiparticle effects and, specifically, in "giant" multiexciton interaction energies.

articleTitle: Threshold conditions for a random laser mode
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Random lasers are simplest miniature sources of stimulated emission without cavity. The developed model adequately describes the dependence of threshold pumping energy density versus radius of the pumped spot, which is experimentally obtained in Nd/sub 0.5/La/sub 0.5/Al/sub 3/(BO/sub 3/)/sub 4/ scattering ceramic.

articleTitle: Symmetry change of a nonlinear optical response of a porous silicon birefringent photonic structure
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: This paper presents the fabrication of an anisotropic photonic crystal and studies its nonlinear optical response and symmetry by means of optical harmonic generation. Hence, the significance of photonic band structure for nonlinear optical processes is demonstrated. This work also provides with a new recipe to affect /spl chi//sup (3)/ nonlinearity and its symmetry in silicon-based structure.

articleTitle: Optical switching in an organic semiconductor microcavity in the polariton regime
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Nonlinear optical response is reported in organic semiconductor microcavities operating in the strongly coupled polariton regime, with thin films of cyanine J-aggregates sandwiched between low-loss dielectric mirrors. The delocalized excitons are subject to large polariton "Rabi" splittings and modulated by near resonant fsec excitation pulses.

articleTitle: Ultrasmall channel add/drop devices based on in-plane proportional hetero photonic crystals
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We propose a new concept of "in-plane proportional hetero photonic crystals (PCs)" to obtain optimum performance of PC-based devices at multiple wavelengths. Ultrasmall channel add/drop device is successfully demonstrated based on the concept.

articleTitle: Electromagnetically induced absorption due to transfer of coherence and to transfer of population
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A new type of electromagnetically induced absorption in degenerate two-level systems is proposed. It occurs for parallelly polarized fields when collisional transfer of population from the ground state exceeds that from the excited state.

articleTitle: Complex photonic systems with external control: from optical NTC resistance to tunable random laser action
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We will discuss the transport of optical waves in complex photonic systems. In particular we will go into the possibilities of tuning complex optical devices via liquid crystal infiltration. Tuning of ordered systems like photonic bandgap crystals is being exploited in various ways. We will discuss the possibilities that disordered dielectrics offer. As a special example we will discuss the tunable random laser.

articleTitle: Single beam polarization tomography: fourth order approach
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present the new experimental technique of measuring all polarization parameters of the single frequency-spatial mode of the optical fields in the fourth order approach. We experimentally studied several classical and nonclassical states of the single-mode field.

articleTitle: Engineering quantum phases of cold atoms
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We will discuss how cold atoms in optical lattices could be used for probing physics of quantum phase transitions. Examples include probing the origin of high temperature superconductivity, controlling quantum magnetic phenomena and "engineering" exotic quantum phases.

articleTitle: Measurement of the 9S level lifetime in francium
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We measure the lifetime of the 9S state in francium through its decay to the 7P3/2 state using two photon excitation and time-correlated single-photon counting techniques. We obtain a lifetime of 107.53/spl plusmn/0.94 ns.

articleTitle: Nanoscale quantum-dot light-emitting diodes
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We compare several approaches to the fabrication of nanoscale quantum-dot LEDs for single-photon applications, including shadow-mask and oxide-confined structures. Strong carrier localization in the dots allows us to demonstrate efficient submicrometer-sized LEDs.

articleTitle: Interaction of coherent beams in Kerr nonlinear waveguide arrays
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report experiments on beam interactions in nonlinear discrete waveguide arrays. Phase sensitive spatial scanning for medium powers and energy exchange between spatially separated beams across three guides for high powers was observed.

articleTitle: Optical trapping and Raman spectroscopy of single living cells and single organelles
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate that single living cells and single organelles within a cell can be manipulated with a near-infrared beam and Raman spectra of the trapped particles can be collected to offer biochemical composition for rapid identification of microorganisms and real-time analysis.

articleTitle: A nanophotonic switch: transient dynamics and switching operation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The operation of a nanophotonic switch was investigated theoretically. An increase in the exciton population with fast vibrations was obtained in the state-filling condition. We also found that the population decay time can be shortened by changing the state-filling time.

articleTitle: Localization of light in optically-induced gratings
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We study experimentally nonlinear localization of light in refractive index gratings optically induced in a photorefractive crystal. We demonstrate generation of spatial solitons and their bound states, similar to those observed in optical waveguide arrays.

articleTitle: Cold Rydberg atoms and plasmas in strong magnetic fields
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We describe our theoretical and experimental efforts to understand cold Rydberg atom gases and plasmas in strong magnetic fields.

articleTitle: Bose-Einstein condensates in one-dimensional optical lattices: bandgap structure and solitons
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present a theory of the band-gap spectrum and nonlinear localization of a Bose-Einstein condensate in 1D optical lattices and superlattices. The theory extends beyond the usual single-band and tight-binding approximations.

articleTitle: A new inverse scattering algorithm for reconstructing highly reflecting fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate a new inverse-scattering algorithm for reconstructing highly reflecting fiber Bragg gratings, used in optical communication systems, that could not be studied before from a reflection spectrum sampled with a practical bandwidth and resolution.

articleTitle: 3D and 2D silicon photonic crystals for microphotonic circuits
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Photonic crystals might offer a unique solution for building ultradense photonic integrated circuits. Recent achievements in fabrication of silicon photonic crystals compatible with microelectronics processing will be reported.

articleTitle: Efficient coupling of radiation into guided slab resonances through two-dimensional photonic crystal
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Coupling of radiation to /spl Gamma/ point photonic crystal resonances is explored through photoluminescence measurements. Photoluminescence from a quantum well embedded in a two-dimensional photonic crystal is enhanced by resonant fields. Experiments and simulations are compared.

articleTitle: Pattern formation in an incoherent cavity
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report the first experimental observation of pattern-formation in a nonlinear cavity for which the circulating light is both spatially and temporally incoherent. The pattern-formation process is associated with two consecutive thresholds: one when self-focusing overcomes diffraction and the other when feedback overcomes losses.

articleTitle: Anomalous dispersion of transparent two-, three- and four-level ensembles
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. A comparative theoretical analysis of the strongly driven and the degenerate two-level system, two closely spaced gain lines, and two different double-lambda-schemes is given with respect to their performance as negative dispersive transparent media.

articleTitle: Increasing the guiding bandwidth of photonic crystal waveguides by perturbing the periodicity
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Flattening of the guided modes of photonic crystal waveguides limits the guiding bandwidth. This behavior is caused by the periodicity of the structures and can be modified by perturbing it. We present a new waveguide design which allows guiding over the entire photonic band gap.

articleTitle: Observation of hydrodynamic expansion of a strongly-interacting Fermi gas: signature of superfluidity?
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We observe dramatic anisotropic expansion of a strongly-interacting Fermi gas upon release from an optical trap. The observed hydrodynamic behavior is a possible first signature of the onset of a new type of high-temperature superfluidity.

articleTitle: Forced evaporative cooling in a holographic atom trap
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We present progress on evaporative cooling of rubidium atoms in a holographic atom trap. Adiabatically decreasing the intensity of our YAG laser results in phase space densities greater than 1/2.

articleTitle: Emission in the ballistic propagation regime of colloidal photonic crystals
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Luminescent CdTe nanocrystals were integrated with thin opal films. Increase of the saturation threshold in a photonic bandgap was interpreted in terms of emission stimulation. Modeling of resonating inhomogeneous eigenmodes justified the bandgap emission properties.

articleTitle: Quantum and classical aspects of coincidence imaging
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We discuss the differences between classical and quantum sources in the context of coincidence imaging.

articleTitle: Stark manipulation of the free radical OH
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Our latest work towards utilizing Stark deceleration on a beam of molecular free radicals is presented. Observed signal enhancement using hexapole focusing and the necessary phase space matching conditions are discussed.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of quantum ellipsometry
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the feasibility of entangled-photon quantum ellipsometry using semiconductor samples.

articleTitle: Manipulating individual atoms in microscopic optical dipole traps
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have realized very small optical dipole traps to store and manipulate individual atoms. Due to the small trap volume, a "collisional blockade" mechanism limits the number of trapped atoms to 1 over a large range of loading rates. We have studied this collisional blockade effect, and measured the oscillation frequencies and temperature of a single trapped atom, that appears to be in the sub-Doppler regime. Various mechanisms for turner cooling will be described, as well as the perspectives for using this system for quantum information processing.

articleTitle: Nonlinear solitary waves in an electro-magnetically induced nonlinear waveguide
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Possibility of the propagation of nonlinear solitary waves in an electro-magnetically induced transparency atomic medium is shown. A coupling light is found to induce a nonlinear waveguide in the medium, and the solitary waves can be freely controlled in the waveguide.

articleTitle: Dynamical instabilities in an attractive Bose-Einstein condensate with a vortex
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A Bose-Einstein condensate with a vortex has dynamical instability, when the attractive interaction between atoms exceeds a critical value. The vortex splits into two clusters, which unite to restore the original vortex or collapse.

articleTitle: Motional quantum state reconstruction in an optical lattice
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We demonstrate reconstruction of the quantum center-of-mass motion of laser-cooled atoms confined in an optical lattice. We examine time-evolution of the density matrix to study decoherence effects in the lattice.

articleTitle: Wave propagation in periodically-curved waveguides: the quantum-mechanical analogy
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The properties of beam propagation in a periodically-curved optical waveguide beyond the usual perturbative approach are theoretically studied. The existence of unusual and exotic effects, such as dynamic beam splitting, dynamic directional coupling, and reduction of radiation losses are also shown. These unusual and exotic effects are fully similar to the phenomena of dynamic wave function stabilization, ionization quenching and wavepacket dichotomy encountered in multiphoton radiation-matter processes with super-intense and high-frequency laser fields.

articleTitle: Design of high-Q photonic crystal optical cavities through Fourier space methods
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: By describing radiation losses through a Fourier space picture of modal couplings, low loss photonic crystal cavities are designed using a group theory-based analysis and finite-difference time-domain calculations, resulting in predicted quality factors exceeding 10/sup 5/.

articleTitle: Secure key generation using bounded-sampling of a chaotic semiconductor laser
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have demonstrated secure key generation based on practical physical limits of continuous data acquisition of a rapidly fluctuating random signal generated by a chaotic semiconductor laser and transmitted over an optical fiber.

articleTitle: Exciton polariton emission enhancement in semiconductor microcavities containing an optically induced electron gas
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present a study of a microcavity polariton system in the presence of an optically induced electron gas. Angle resolved photoluminescence measurements with nonresonant excitation show enhanced emission from the k /spl ap/ 0 states as the electron density is increased. This indicates that electron-polariton scattering can assist in relaxing the polariton bottleneck.

articleTitle: Nanoparticle-sensor based on optical gradient force
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present a detection scheme for nanoscale particles based on the optical gradient force and torque near a tightly focused laser beam. The focus affects the path of nanoparticles passing by and a quadrant detector records the particle trajectory. A feedback system continuously adjusts the laser power thereby preventing the particles from being trapped. Particle size and shape can be assessed by evaluating the time-trace of the quadrant detector signal.

articleTitle: Plasmon-assisted transmission of quantum entanglement
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We investigate whether entanglement is conserved when polarization entangled photons are converted to surface plasmons, propagating along subwavelength metal hole arrays. We find that entanglement survives, but is limited by spatial dispersion of the hole arrays.

articleTitle: Near cutoff behaviors of high-order harmonic generation from molecular gases
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The near cutoff behaviors of high-order harmonic generation (HHG) from molecular gases is investigated. Results reveal that harmonic cutoff is extended only for molecules that show ionization suppression. Another interesting result is that the HHG intensity drops slower in N/sub 2/ and O/sub 2/, while in Ar there is a sharp drop at the cutoff. This phenomena could be induced by the molecule orientation in the laser field.

articleTitle: The operational criterion of the orthogonality of single-mode biphotons
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present an operational criterion for polarization orthogonality of single-mode biphoton field, which allows us to experimentally distinguish one state from the variety of orthogonal ones. Such a criterion can be applied to the realization of the three-state quantum cryptography protocols. The experimental verification of the criterion leads to the observation of the anticorrelation effect for the orthogonal biphotons in arbitrary polarization states.

articleTitle: Quantum degenerate Fermi and Bose gases
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We present our experiments performed in Paris on a quantum degenerate mixture of lithium 6 (fermion) and lithium 7 (boson) atoms. The perspective of reaching the BCS transition on the fermionic component using a Feshbach resonance is discussed.

articleTitle: Single-photon and two-photon wavepackets spontaneous parametric down-conversion
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Single-photon (first-order coherence) and two-photon (second-order coherence) wavepackets of entangled two-photon states in spontaneous parametric down-conversion fields are calculated and demonstrated experimentally.

articleTitle: Linear mode locking and the structure of lasing modes in random lasers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. The aim of this study is to re-evaluate the relation between the properties of normal modes of the passive component of the lasing medium and characteristics of the laser oscillations such as lasing threshold, or the spatial structure of the lasing modes.

articleTitle: Experimental implementation of Hardy's paradox
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Hardy's paradox, previously unamenable to direct experimental test, brings to light some of the striking difficulties in the interpretation of indirect quantum measurements. Using a newly developed 'photon switch,' we implement this proposal.

articleTitle: Optical bistability in photonic crystal systems
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Using an analytical theory and detailed computational experiments, we predict surprising optical bistability behavior in various photonic crystal systems.

articleTitle: Determining the carrier-envelope frequency and phase by few-cycle nonlinear optics in semiconductors
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We discuss semiconductor nonlinear optics in the nonperturbative few-cycle regime. In particular, we introduce "camouflage third-harmonic generation" and speculate about the possibility to determine the CEO phase itself.

articleTitle: Femtosecond intersubband dynamics of electrons in AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Ultrafast electron dynamics in the inversion layer of an AlGaN/GaN transistor is studied in pump-probe experiments with 50-fs midinfrared pulses, e1-e2 intersubband scattering and thermalization occur within 200 fs.

articleTitle: A fast, deterministic source of single Cr atoms
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We produce single Cr atoms on demand by feedback control of loading and loss from a magneto-optical trap. We observe single-atom occupation probabilities of over 98% and efficient ejection at rates up to 10 Hz.

articleTitle: Cold-atom funnel using near-field light
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We observed the output of Rb atoms from a near-field optical funnel. A beam flux of 10/sup 5/ atoms/cm/sup 2/ is obtained by performing Sisyphus cooling under blue detuning of +1 GHz.

articleTitle: Approaching quantum-limited cw anti-Stokes conversion cavity-enhanced Raman-resonant four-wave mixing
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Building on previous efficient Raman downconversion achievements, we show that the upconversion efficiency from a continuous-wave pump beam into a single anti-Stokes order can approach the fundamental quantum limit through severe cavity enhancement of Raman-resonant four-wave mixing.

articleTitle: Discrete vector solitons in Kerr nonlinear waveguide arrays
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report the first experimental observation of vector discrete solitons. We find that at appropriate power levels two orthogonally polarized beams collapse into a highly confined vector discrete soliton in spite of the presence of energy exchange due to four-wave-mixing.

articleTitle: Resonant radiative and non-radiative coupling between a molecule and a metallic tip
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We study numerically the radiative and non-radiative decay rates of a molecule close to the apex of a metallic tip. We show that both rates present a resonance at different frequencies which, in general, do not coincide. This behavior is explained by a general model describing the resonant behavior of the electromagnetic response of the tip. We also investigate the influence of a small defect located close to the tip apex. We show that it may substantially modify the ratio between the radiative and non-radiative contributions, and induces a frequency shift of the resonances. This may explain why experiments on single-molecule fluorescence dramatically depend on the tip quality.

articleTitle: Spatio-temporal waveform of focused half-cycle THz pulses
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Spatio-temporal intensity distribution of focused nearly half-cycle THz pulses was observed using a THz imaging setup with an expanded probe beam. Ring-like distribution away from the peak position in space or in time was observed.

articleTitle: Centimeter-size single-domain colloidal crystals on patterned substrates
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report the deposition of colloidal films through electrophoresis on conductive substrates patterned with holographic gratings. We observe long-range hexagonal or square ordering when the particle diameter is commensurate with the grating pitch.

articleTitle: Role of "hidden" variables in generalized synchronization of chaos: experiments on a microchip laser with optoelectronic feedback
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A recorded signal from a chaotic microchip laser repeatedly generates a non-identical response waveform in the identical laser, demonstrating generalized synchronization. The hidden interplay of longitudinal modes produces a complex functional relationship between the waveforms.

articleTitle: Transition from a quantum-dot to a quantum-wire electronic structure in InGaAs/GaAs quantum-dot chains
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report on the carrier transport behaviors observed in a vertically and laterally organized quantum-dot array. Photoluminescence polarization studies show a dual dot/wire electronic structure and a transition between them as the temperature is increased.

articleTitle: Enhancing coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering sensitivity by maximizing quantum coherence
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We develop the enhancement of coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS) in terms of maximizing the coherence by stimulated Raman adiabatic passage and chirped pulse adiabatic rapid passage. This technique can be readily extended to a femtosecond time scale for rapid identification and trace of impurities.

articleTitle: Extremely slow coherent polarization decay of waveguide- plasmon-polaritons in metallic photonic crystal slabs
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Autocorrelation measurements using sub-20 fs laser pulses show that dephasing times of quasiparticles consisting of waveguide modes and particle plasmons can be increased by more than a factor of two when tuning the photonic crystal slab into the strong coupling regime.

articleTitle: Generation of polarization entanglement from a PPKTP parametric downconverter
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have generated polarization-entangled photon pairs from a type-II phase-matched periodically poled KTP parametric downconverter with collinear outputs. Bell's inequality was violated with a value of 2.57 /spl plusmn/ 0.03.

articleTitle: Exciton-biexciton coherent coupling effects on exciton absorption in quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The absorption characteristics of an exciton-biexciton system are examined for quantum dots by single-dot photoluminescence spectroscopy and theoretical calculation based on the density-matrix method. Exciton-biexciton coherent interaction is found to markedly vary exciton absorption spectra.

articleTitle: Control of quantum correlation between frequency bands in ultrashort pulses via nonlinear fiber propagation and pulse shaping
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Novel fiber-based schemes for controlling quantum correlation between frequency bands to generate photon-number squeezing and quadrature two-mode squeezing are studied. The scheme is based on a nonlinear fiber, a pulse shaper, and an adaptive feedback loop. Experimental results of photon-number squeezing are presented.

articleTitle: Probing charge carriers in semiconductor quantum dots by terahertz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The terahertz response of photo-excited charge carriers in CdSe quantum dots has been studied. Quantum dots containing a single electron-hole pair exhibit a real polarizability with a magnitude exceeding 10000 /spl Aring//sup 3/.

articleTitle: Hamiltonian formulation for light propagation in waveguide-microresonator structures
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present a Hamiltonian description of the optical properties of structures composed of channel waveguides and microresonators. From the Hamiltonian we extract highly accurate formulae for the dispersion relation of the structures.

articleTitle: Laser cooling of atoms and molecules via optical shaking
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We propose a novel generic approach to laser cooling based on non-resonant interactions with optical standing waves experiencing random sudden phase jumps. The technique, termed "optical shaking", is applicable to the cooling of atoms and molecules to high phase space densities and without the loss of particles typical of evaporative cooling.

articleTitle: Trapping a soliton by localized gain in a lossy fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A model of nonlinear fiber grating with a "hot spot", which combines loss with locally applied gain and increment of refractive index, is introduced. Solutions for pinned solitons are found analytically. Their stability and collisions of moving solitons with the hot spot are investigated numerically.

articleTitle: Zero-phonon linewidth in self-assembled CdSe quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: High-resolution spectral hole burning studies in self-assembled CdSe/ZnSe quantum dots reveal a sharp zero-phonon line as well as contributions due to acoustic phonon- and optical phonon-assisted transitions. Zero-phonon linewidth of a few /spl mu/eV is obtained.

articleTitle: Coherent dynamics of optically-inactive excitons in semiconductor quantum wells
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Ultrafast coherent dynamics of optically-inactive excitons in photo-excited quantum wells are investigated. The exciton momentum distribution follows an interesting moving pattern driven by the Coulomb coupling between the interband polarization and excitons with non-zero momenta.

articleTitle: Extremely thin cell for laser spectroscopy with smoothly variable thickness of atomic vapor column in the range 140-1700 nm
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: An extremely thin cell with smoothly variable thickness of Rb atomic vapor column in the range 140-1700 nm has been developed. New possible applications for laser spectroscopy are presented.

articleTitle: Spin relaxation in [110] and [001] InAs/GaSb superlattices
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A 25 times enhancement of the electron spin lifetime is observed in a [110] InAs/GaSb superlattice relative to the corresponding [001] superlattice, an effect that is primarily attributed to suppression of native interface asymmetry.

articleTitle: Optically induced biexciton energy shift in semiconductor quantum wells
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The energy level shift of a coherent biexciton (bound two-exciton state) in a semiconductor has been observed experimentally and analyzed theoretically. The shift, which results from the presence of excitons, can be related to the AC Stark shifts of the underlying exciton states.

articleTitle: Single-photon source and quantum memory
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have experimentally demonstrated a new kind of single-photon source and a cyclical quantum memory device for photonic qubits. These initial experiments involved storage loops, active switching, and parametric down-conversion photon pairs.

articleTitle: Cavity-QED atoms and photons on demand
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Cavity QED allows one to manipulate the motion of an observed atom with real-time feedback. Single photons emitted on demand exhibit second-order interference, a prerequisite for all-optical quantum information processing.

articleTitle: Observation of huge nonlinear absorption enhancement near exciton resonance in GaN
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Huge nonlinear-absorption enhancement was observed in GaN system at the excitonic transition wavelength. This excitonic enhancement is attributed to four-wave-mixing type nonlinear processes. The peak nonlinear coefficient is at least 3000 cm/GW corresponding to an enhancement factor of >200. The dephasing time of the exciton was also observed to be 60-160 fs in GaN thin film at room temperature.

articleTitle: Pattern formation and spatial solitons in bistable liquid-crystal microcavities
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report on spatial pattern formation, and appearances of 'optical bullet holes' in single-mode microcavities that are filled with liquid-crystals, when pumped above the cavity resonance frequency. These phenomena only occur beyond the bistability threshold.

articleTitle: Optical realization of the quantum 3-box problem
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Using an optical three-rail interferometer, we have implemented Aharonov and Vaidman's "quantum box problem". This provides interesting insight into measurement, probability, and nonlocality in quantum mechanics.

articleTitle: Carrier-envelope control of femtosecond lasers with attosecond timing jitter
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have demonstrated long-term control of the carrier-envelope offset (CEO) with only 10 attosecond timing jitter and discuss the physical origin of the CEO fluctuations and the increased CEO phase noise due to additional external spectral broadening in a microstructure fiber.

articleTitle: Numerical calculations of enhanced transmission through sub-wavelength apertures
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Finite difference time domain (FDTD) solutions of Maxwell's equations are presented which reveal the nature of the recent observation of anomalously high optical transmission through metal films with sub-wavelength apertures in surface corrugations.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optics in the angstrom regime: hard X-ray frequency doubling in perfect crystals
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Based on the dynamical diffraction theory, we discuss a second harmonic generation with hard X-rays. We show that the multiple scattering effects lead to a generation of two coupled second harmonic waves propagating in the forward and scattering direction. The possibility to phase-match the process is shown. Modeling of a frequency doubling experiment suggests that harmonic signal should be measurable for X-ray pumping with ps-pulses of mJ energy.

articleTitle: Enhanced spontaneous emission from colloidal quantum dots embedded in a monolithic microcavity
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate an enhancement of the spontaneous emission from colloidal quantum dots embedded in a half-wavelength 1D cavity. Compared to free space, the emission of the dots is enhanced by a factor of 2.7.

articleTitle: Collision of gap solitons in fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Results of a systematic study of collisions between moving solitons in fiber grating are presented. Various outcomes of the collision are identified, the most interesting one being merger of the solitons into a single zero-velocity pulse.

articleTitle: Ultrafast electron dynamics in silver nanoparticle arrays
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present the results of ultrafast optical experiments on silver quantum dot super-lattices. Dramatic changes in the electron dynamics occur as a function of interparticle spacing due to enhanced dipolar coupling and, most importantly, electron delocalization.

articleTitle: Anomalous dispersion in one-dimensional photonic band gap structures with birefringent layers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Anomalous dispersion in biaxial birefringent one dimensional photonic structures has been studied This causes the Poynting vector to reverse its direction with respect to the wave vector, with consequent manifestation of negative refraction. Conditions to enhance the effects are discussed.

articleTitle: Coherent optical manipulation of quantum dot electron spins
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report on the coherent optical manipulation of electron spins in the ground state of charged quantum dots. The measured spin coherence time is limited by the distribution of g-factors, but exceeds one nanosecond.

articleTitle: Generation of spatially coherent light at 13 nm using quasi phase-matching in modulated hollow fibers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present measurements of the spatial coherence of extreme ultraviolet radiation at 13 nm. The measured spatial coherence is unity near the center of the beam.

articleTitle: Coherent control of optically injected population and spin in (111)-GaAs
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate independent coherent control of population and spin in (111)-grown GaAs through quantum interference of one- and two-photon absorption of /spl sim/100 fs phase-locked pulses with various polarization combinations and crystal orientations.

articleTitle: Variation of spectral content of subcycle far-infrared pulses due to phase-amplitude modulation in near-field diffraction
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Spectral content of subcycle electromagnetic pulses is not conserved under phase shift of the carrier with respect to the pulse envelope. We observe carrier-phase dependent large variation of the low frequency content of subcycle far-infrared (terahertz) pulses in the near-field zone of a subwavelength aperture.

articleTitle: Nonlinear spectroscopy of a charged GaAs quantum dot ensemble
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
