abstract: Time and frequency domain nonlinear spectroscopy measurements on a charged GaAs quantum dot ensemble identify negatively charged excitons. Spectral hole burning suggests not all states are strongly localized.

articleTitle: Very efficient direct third harmonic generation in nanostructured ZnO films
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: This study presents the very strong third-order nonlinear optical coefficient of nanostructured ZnO thin films. Hence, it is possible to directly generate third harmonic of ultrashort pulses with efficiency of several percent.

articleTitle: Ultrafast carrier dynamics in tunneling injection quantum dot lasers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have performed differential transmission spectroscopy measurements on tunneling-injection quantum dot lasers and directly measured a temperature-independent tunneling time of /spl sim/2 ps. Rate equations using measured parameters gave an excellent fit to actual device performance.

articleTitle: Broad-spectrum frequency comb generation and carrier-envelope offset frequency measurement using the second harmonic generation of a mode-locked fiber laser
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Frequency comb spanning more than one octave has been achieved by injecting the second harmonic generation (780 nm) of a mode-locked fiber laser (1.56 /spl mu/m) into a photonic crystal fiber. We propose and realize a novel interferometric scheme for observing the carrier-envelope offset frequency.

articleTitle: Near-field scanning optical microscopy of photonic crystal high-Q nanocavities
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Near-field scanning optical microscopy (NSOM) was used to observe high-resolution images of planar photonic crystal nanocavities fabricated in active InGaAsP material. We have observed the smallest optical cavity modes and dielectric band modes.

articleTitle: Very efficient multi-photon absorption in porphyrins with extended /spl pi/-conjugation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report a dramatic enhancement of multiphoton absorption in porphyrins in near-infrared range. This is achieved by the near-resonance conditions for each photon to be absorbed and by an extension of molecular /spl pi/-conjugation.

articleTitle: Passive optical amplifier for picosecond and femtosecond pulses
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The coherent superposition of mode-locked pulses stored in a passive optical cavity results in a single amplified pulse when switched out. Theoretical and experimental results demonstrate superior performance when compared with active cavity dumping techniques.

articleTitle: Trapping and storing light in /spl chi//sup (2)/ photonic crystals
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A study of parametric down-conversion in photonic crystals reveals that the probe field can be slowed down to 11 m/s: i.e. a tunneling velocity previously reported only for coherently resonant interactions in Bose-Einstein condensates.

articleTitle: Cooper pair breaking and superconducting state recovery dynamics in MgB/sub 2/ probed by time-resolved THz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We measured the Cooper pair breaking and condensate recovery dynamics in MgB/sub 2/ by means of time-resolved optical pump-terahertz probe spectroscopy. The observed photoexcitation intensity dependence of Cooper-pair breaking is attributed to the presence of two superconducting gaps in MgB/sub 2/.

articleTitle: Random laser thresholds in pulsed and cw regimes
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We show that the threshold pumping density measured in random lasers at the appearance of the first giant spike of stimulated emission can be much different from that calculated in cw regime.

articleTitle: Polarization superprism effect in surface plasmon polaritonic nanostructures
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Polarization effects in surface plasmon polaritonic crystals (two-dimensional photonic crystals on a metal surface) are observed in the optical transmission of metallic nanostructures and the directional switching between line-defect waveguides. This new effect can be regarded as a polarization-domain analog of the spectral superprism effect in photonic crystals.

articleTitle: Bright source of polarization-entangled photons using periodically poled potassium titanyl phosphate (KTP)
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We used two perpendicular crystals of periodically-poled potassium titanyl phosphate (KTP) to efficiently generate frequency-nondegenerate, polarization-entangled photons in a single spatial mode. The source is compact, inexpensive, and suitable for long-distance fiber-based quantum communication.

articleTitle: Dynamics and emission of femtosecond laser-induced plasma inclusion in water droplets
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Femtosecond laser pulses can cause water droplets to emit a backward white light continuum attributed to microscopic plasma inclusions. Pump experiments have been undertaken to enlighten the laser induced plasma formation via forward elastic scattering.

articleTitle: Electron-polariton scattering in n-doped semiconductor microcavities
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. In semiconductor microcavities, electron-polariton scattering has been proposed as an efficient process that can drive polaritons from the bottleneck region to the ground state, achieving Bose amplification of the optical emission. We present first experimental observation of this process in a structure that allows control of electron density. A substantial enhancement of photoluminescence is also reported under the optimal configuration. We show that this enhancement is more effective at higher temperatures due to the different way that the dispersion relation controls electron scattering processes that either broaden or relax polaritons.

articleTitle: Virtual-real interference in a dense potassium vapor
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We investigate the interference between virtual and real population amplitudes in a dense potassium vapor using transient four-wave mixing with shaped pulses. Results for the D/sub 1/ line agree with theory, but D/sub 2/ results behave anomalously.

articleTitle: Sonography: a new method to measure laser filaments in air
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. The sound emitted from a filament was measured using a microphone. A model describes the sound emission mechanism, which allows to retrieve the light intensity as well as the free electron density in the filament.

articleTitle: Single quantum dot photodiodes: Rabi-flops in a two level system with electric contacts
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: On the basis of a single semiconductor quantum dot incorporated in a photodiode we have succeeded in preparing a two-level system with electric contacts, a setup which was previously not attained on the basis of other two-level systems. By means of such a single quantum dot photodiode we demonstrate the transfer of coherent optical excitations into deterministic photocurrents. Rabi oscillations are shown to be directly reflected in the photocurrent. For optical excitation with pi-pulses we observe a quantitative photocurrent given by I=f /spl times/ e, where f is the repetition frequency of the experiment and e is the elementary charge.

articleTitle: Generation of light carrying orbital angular momentum via induced coherence grating in cold atom
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Light carrying orbital angular momentum is generated via an electromagnetically induced Zeeman coherence grating in cold cesium atoms. This constitutes a first step towards the processing of quantum information encoded in a multidimensional state space.

articleTitle: Stability and excitation of gap solitons in binary waveguide arrays
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We analyze gap solitons in the engineered binary waveguide arrays including their existence and stability. We demonstrate that the spatial gap solitons can be efficiently generated by two interfering Gaussian input beams.

articleTitle: Imaging intramolecular energy transfer in conjugated polymers by single chain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report on the time resolved polarized emission from individual conjugated polymer chains as a function of temperature. Besides observing intrachain energy transfer in real time, we can also infer dephasing times from homogeneous linewidths.

articleTitle: 12-fs, diode-pumped Cr/sup 3+/:LiCAF laser
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: 12-fs-pulses from a diode-pumped, soft-aperture Kerr-lens mode-locked Cr/sup 3+/:LiCAF laser with a spectral bandwidth of 143 nm, 25 mW of output power at a repetition rate of 112 MHz are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Fs time-resolved selective control of multilevel systems using optical interference
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A new selective excitation technique using a superposition of two identical frequency-chirped pulses is demonstrated. By adjusting the time delay between the two pulses, a selected transition of the Rb doublet was brought into the "holes" of the interference pattern and remained nonexcited, thus allowing to manipulate another transition by the laser field as if it is an isolated two-level system.

articleTitle: Single molecule spectroscopy of multichromophoric assemblies
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have investigated multichromophoric assemblies composed of a variable number of chromophores by single molecule spectroscopy. Specific spectral signatures have allowed to distinguish at the single molecule level between molecular dimers representing strong and weak electronic dipole-dipole coupling. By using fluorescence excitation spectroscopy at low temperature, the sharp purely electronic zero-phonon lines of single chromophores within a single dendrimer containing four chromophores could be isolated in the frequency domain.

articleTitle: On the general form of dark states in "atoms+quantized field" system
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Recent outstanding experiments on light pulse storage in resonant atomic media have opened a new promising direction in quantum information processing. One of basic concepts is the dark state polariton, which can be considered as a dark state of atoms in a field of one coherent and one quantized modes. Motivated by these results, this study tries to find the most general form of dark states in a combined system "atoms+quantized field".

articleTitle: Violation of single parameter scaling in random periodic-on-average systems
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Localization properties of random periodic-on-average systems are studied. It is shown that the statistics of states within and outside of original conductance bands are completely different. A new scaling behavior of the latter states is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Cavity QED with an optical lattice; towards quantum feedback with atomic detuning
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The incorporation of an optical lattice in a cavity QED system increases the number of parameters available for quantum feedback.

articleTitle: Near-field functional field transformation structures
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Irregular wavelength-scale transformation structures offer potential for wavelength division multiplexing and laser mode control. A microwave waveguide experiment demonstrates for the first time wavelength-dependent mode conversion. Optical realization using silicon processing is facilitated by lift-off.

articleTitle: Experimental phase-sensitive cloning
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Phase sensitive cloning achieves higher fidelity than the universal cloner by restricting cloning to linear polarization states. The experimental results are presented for two nonorthogonal bases of a weak coherent beam.

articleTitle: Quantum key distribution over distances as long as 101 km
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate, for the first time, quantum key distribution over 101 km of standard telecom fibre. The system is characterized by a quantum bit error rate of /spl sim/7.1% and a bit rate of 15 Hz.

articleTitle: Megavolt discharges triggered and guided with laser filaments
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Long ionized channels appear as a result of nonlinear propagation of femtosecond terawatt pulses. We demonstrate the ability of such filament bundles to trigger and guide megavolt discharges across a gap up to 3.8 m.

articleTitle: Single-photon emission from highly uniform site-controlled semiconductor quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We observed anti-bunching of photons emitted from (In)GaAs/AlGaAs quantum dots grown on pyramidal recess patterns. The control on dot position, photon energy (1.43-1.65 eV) and small inhomogeneous broadening (10 meV) make them useful in practical single-photon emitters.

articleTitle: Tunnel-coupled quantum dots: atomistic theory of quantum dot molecules and arrays
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The electronic structure and optical properties of quantum dot molecules and arrays are determined by use of atomistic tight-binding theory. Electron states follow the artificial molecule analogy. Hole levels are much more complex.

articleTitle: Temperature-dependent carrier distributions and level degeneracy in self-assembled quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Femtosecond spectroscopy is used to study the transparency conditions in In/sub 0.4/Ga/sub 0.6/As self-organized quantum dots. The spatial degeneracy of excited state is experimentally observed and a multilevel model is shown to be consistent with the temperature-dependent behavior.

articleTitle: Resonantly enhanced blackbody radiation from a periodic array of microcavities
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Blackbody radiation can be controlled by using a periodic array of microcavities on the surface. Thermal radiation is found to be resonantly enhanced by three different mechanisms depending on the aperture ratio of the periodic array.

articleTitle: Near-field, phase-sensitive spectroscopy of metal nanoassemblies
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We study amplitude and phase responses of individual gold nanoparticles and nanoparticle dimers by applying near-field illumination with a bright, broad-band, femtosecond, white-light continuum.

articleTitle: Ultrafast coherent vibrational response of intermolecular hydrogen bonded molecular complexes in solution
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Coherent vibrational motions along intermolecular hydrogen bonds are observed in mid-infrared pump-probe and photon echo experiments. The underlying low-frequency modes couple anharmonically to the O-H stretching mode and dephase much slower than the O-H stretching mode.

articleTitle: Characterization of channel add/drop functions using donor/acceptor point defects in two dimensional photonic crystal slabs
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Channel add/drop functions using donor/acceptor point defects in two dimensional photonic crystal slabs are quantitatively investigated and compared. Spectral width of donor defect is found to be much narrower than that of acceptor defect.

articleTitle: Dynamical localization in microcylinder lasers with surface roughness
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate that the scattering effect of the surface roughness in semiconductor microdisk lasers is strongly suppressed by dynamical Anderson localization. This phenomenon allows for lasing action on quasi-regular modes in samples with surface defects, in agreement with experimental observations.

articleTitle: Super-Poissonian intensity fluctuations and correlations between pump and probe fields in electromagnetically induced transparency
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We measured intensity fluctuations of pump and probe beams after interaction with Rb atoms in electromagnetically induced transparency. Both fields presented super-Poissonian statistics and become correlated in intensity, in qualitative agreement with theoretical predictions. The measured correlation is a first step towards the observation of macroscopic entanglement in ElT.

articleTitle: Chaos-assisted tunneling in microlasers with partially chaotic resonators
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate that in lasers with non-integrable resonators, chaos-assisted tunneling leads to dramatic changes in the emission spectrum, removing the near-degeneracy of symmetry-related doublets and changing the lifetimes of high-Q modes by several orders of magnitude. Our theory is in quantitative agreement with numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Decay of an ultracold fermionic lithium gas near a Feshbach resonance
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We studied the magnetic field dependence of the inelastic decay of an ultracold, optically trapped fermionic /sup 6/Li gas of different spin compositions. The spin mixture of the two lowest hyperfine states showed two decay resonances at 550 G and 680 G, consistent with the predicted Feshbach resonances for elastic s-wave collisions. The observed lifetimes of several hundred milliseconds are much longer than the expected time for Cooper pair formation and the phase transition to superfluidity in the vicinity of the Feshbach resonance.

articleTitle: Characterization of an octave spanning geometry Ti:sapphire laser
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We directly stabilize the carrier-envelope phase for a conventional geometry, octave spanning, Kerr-lens mode-locked Ti:sapphire laser. Beam characteristics of the continuum are presented.

articleTitle: Quantum imaging versus its classical simulation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Differences between two-photon imaging and its classical simulation are discussed. Quantum entanglement allows simultaneous momentum-momentum and position-position correlations. A quantum image may have spatial resolution beyond the diffraction limit. Classical simulations can never achieve that.

articleTitle: Enhanced total internal reflection by an active medium
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Totally internal reflected beam can be amplified if the lower-index medium has gain. We examine the energy flux and the Goos Manchen shift for various cases.

articleTitle: Decelerating and trapping molecules with time-varying electric fields
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A polar molecule experiences a force in an inhomogeneous electric field. Using this force, neutral molecules can he decelerated and trapped Using a series of 64 pulsed inhomogeneous electric fields ammonia molecules are decelerated and loaded into an electrostatic quadrupole trap or a storage ring.

articleTitle: Measurement of the mean-field interaction in a strongly-interacting Fermi gas
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We release a strongly-interacting, two-component Fermi gas from an optical trap. From the release energy, we determine an important, universal many-body parameter: the ratio of the mean-field energy to the local Fermi energy.

articleTitle: Effect of atomic density on wavepacket motion of atoms in an optical lattice
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We investigate the dependence of oscillations of atoms trapped in an optical lattice on the atomic density. Our observations reflect a non-linear internal feedback mechanism.

articleTitle: Microcavity-enhanced second- and third-harmonic generation in all-silicon photonic crystals
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Simultaneous enhancement of quasi-phase-matched second- and third-harmonic generation is observed in porous silicon photonic-crystal microcavities both in frequency and wave vector domains.

articleTitle: Simplified setup for high-resolution spectroscopy using ultrashort pulses
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Using a broadband femtosecond laser and simple optics, we demonstrate narrow-bandwidth tunable selective vibrational excitation in liquids. The resolution obtained is 80 times higher than the laser bandwidth-the highest obtained from a femtosecond laser to date.

articleTitle: Photoluminescence excitation spectra in T-shaped quantum wires
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We measured polarization-dependent photoluminescence-excitation spectra, of high-quality T-shaped quantum wires at 5 K, and revealed absorption line shape of one-dimensional (1D) continuum and exciton states resulted from strong ID Coulomb interactions.

articleTitle: Demonstration of half waveplate using polarization properties of a photonic crystal
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have constructed and experimentally tested a half waveplate based on the dispersive birefringent properties of a bulk two-dimensional photonic crystal away from its band gap. A polarization contrast better than 200:1 was measured.

articleTitle: Measured signal and group velocity for an optical pulse propagating through a GaAs cavity
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present measurements of the signal and group velocities for chirped optical pulses propagating through a GaAs cavity. Even when measured group velocity becomes negative the measured signal velocity is always less than c/n.

articleTitle: Observation of geometric phase in three-level atoms
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The geometric phases of optically driven atomic wave functions were measured with a photon echo technique in a three-level atomic system. The experimental results match well with simulations using the density matrix.

articleTitle: Electro-optics in a one dimensional photonic crystals
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Electro-optic phase modulation in one-dimensional photonic crystals with the possibility of total internal reflection is investigated. The compactness and other design features of this type of modulation can offer significant advantages over present modulation schemes.

articleTitle: Improved single-photon detector performance
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: High efficiency single-photon detectors are needed for many applications including quantum cryptography and linear-optics quantum computing. We present experimental results showing improved detection efficiency of silicon avalanche photodiodes by reducing reflective losses.

articleTitle: Phase diagram of exciton condensates in coupled quantum wells in-plane traps
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report degenerate exciton condensates in in-plane traps with specially designed coupled quantum wells. The measured phase diagram, size and occupation vs. both temperature and excitation density, suggests a phase transition at a few Kelvin.

articleTitle: Ultra-narrow lasing modes from random amplifying media
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We report experimental observations of ultra-narrow bandwidth (<0.25 nm) random lasing modes in the emission from a suspension of zinc oxide powder in rhodamine 6G. We present, and verify through Monte Carlo simulations, a model that explains the phenomenon.

articleTitle: When one quantum object is measured by another: a new class of quantum paradoxes
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Nearly all quantum experiments involve a classical object (a macroscopic apparatus) measuring a quantum mechanical one (a particle). In the Elitzur-Vaidman bomb-testing experiment the roles have been reversed, and a surprising result ensued. Later, Hardy expanded this method and allowed two and three particles to measure one another before the macroscopic apparatus made the final measurement, obtaining even more intriguing results. Recently, we elaborated this experimental paradigm further, increasing the number of particles that measure one another. The results seem to violate basic notions of space and time. In one experiment, the wave function appears to proceed in space non-sequentially. In the other experiment, entanglement ensues between particles that seem to have never interacted, giving the impression of an inconsistent history. We survey this family of experiments and discuss its implications.

articleTitle: Single mode design and dispersion control of coupled resonator optical waveguides in photonic crystals
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: By engineering a cavity inside a photonic crystal we present a systematic method to engineer the dispersion of a coupled resonator optical waveguide (CROW). By designing a single mode cavity, we demonstrate the design and dispersion control of a single mode CROW in the photonic band gap (PBG).

articleTitle: Bose-Einstein condensates in magnetic waveguides
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We achieved single-mode condensate propagation along homogeneous segments of magnetic waveguides, while waveguide inhomogeneities were observed to fragment the condensate longitudinally. Effects of the nearby microfabricated surface were investigated for magnetically and optically confined condensates.

articleTitle: Nonlinear processes in photonic crystal fibers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Various nonlinear processes in photonic crystal fibers made from fused silica as well as from highly nonlinear glasses are studied, such as 3 octaves broad supercontinua from 0.06 nJ pulses by Cherenkov-like radiation and emission of higher-order solitons, four-wave mixing and stimulated Raman scattering.

articleTitle: Optically sensing the state of a single molecule
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Optical spectroscopy of single molecules senses the state of the molecule through its orientation, lifetime, spectrum, and photon emission statistics. A new class of single-molecule fluorophores may extend the state variables into additional regimes.

articleTitle: Experiments with a science-chamber apparatus for rubidium BEC
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. We report on experiments with a new apparatus for BEC of rubidium, including the transport and manipulation of condensates in a science chamber using optical tweezers, and a study of superradiant scattering in the short-pulse regime.

articleTitle: Fiber cavities for atom chips
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We present experimental realizations of several micro-cavities, constructed from standard fiber optic components, which meet the theoretical criteria for single detection from laser-cooled samples. We discuss integration of these cavities into state-of-the-art 'atom chips'.

articleTitle: Ising- and Bloch walls of phase domains in 2D parametric wave mixing
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report experimental observation and investigation of Ising- and Bloch fronts on boundaries of phase domains appearing in degenerate four wave mixing in a BaTiO/sub 3/-resonator.

articleTitle: Photonic band gap structures in planar nonlinear waveguides: application to squeezing light generation
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Quadrature-amplitude and phase squeezing are investigated in a nonlinear planar waveguide geometry under conditions for which the use of a linear grating fabricated on top of the waveguide reproduces a photonic band gap structures.

articleTitle: Terahertz polaritonics: spectroscopy and technology
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Summary form only given. Coherent phonon-polaritons are generated by femtosecond pulses in electro-optic crystals and exploited for THz spectroscopic and signal processing applications. The use of spatially and temporally shaped excitation fields to generate specified polariton responses the integration of THz waveguides and other functional elements into the polariton host crystals and the use of polaritons for linear and nonlinear THz spectroscopy are discussed.

articleTitle: Evolution of gain in a high-quality single quantum wire laser
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A high quality single quantum wire laser that operates in the 1-D ground state by optical pumping has been achieved. We investigated lasing performance and gain mechanism by using micro-spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Fabrication of three-dimensional photonic crystals with midgap wavelength at 1.55 /spl mu/m
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Seven-functional-layer 3D photonic crystals with midgap wavelength at 1.55 /spl mu/m were fabricated with a layer-by-layer approach. We employed e-beam lithography to align and define the pattern, reactive-ion-etching to transfer the pattern, and spin-on-dielectrics to planarize the surface. Four such cycles were sufficient to complete the fabrication.

articleTitle: Highly directional emission from nearly spherical resonators
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We report highly directional light emission from nearly spherical fused-silica resonators. It is found that non-perturbative phase space structure in the internal ray dynamics profoundly affects evanescent leakage of the whispering-gallery modes.

articleTitle: Raman coherence beats from the entangled exciton Zeeman doublet in a single quantum dot
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The entangled state involving an exciton Zeeman doublet with large entanglement entropy was created using /spl sim/ /spl pi//2 pulses in single GaAs quantum dots. The non-radiative Raman coherence time was determined from quantum beats measured in homodyne detected differential transmission.

articleTitle: Dramatic impact of two photon absorption on multi soliton excitation in non-critically phase-matched biaxial crystals
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally and numerically that strong two photon absorption affects multiple quadratic soliton generation by high power 2D beams in a type-I biaxial crystal (KNbO/sub 3/). Simulations are in a good agreement with the experiment.

articleTitle: Entangled-photon imaging of a phase object
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Previous experimental demonstrations of entangled-photon imaging have been limited to imaging amplitude objects. We report the first experimental results of entangled-photon imaging of a phase object in a reflection configuration.

articleTitle: Intensity and circular polarization correlations of single photons from optically excited semiconductor quantum dots
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We measure experimentally and discuss theoretically the intensity temporal correlations between photons from two different spectral lines that an optically excited single, self-assembled semiconductor quantum dot, emits. Surprisingly, consecutive photons are preferably emitted with the same circular polarization.

articleTitle: Frequency-correlated 1550-nm photon pairs for quantum communication
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We observed frequency correlation of 1550-nm photon pairs generated via broadband parametric downconversion. Wavelength division multiplexing components are used to separate photon pairs into correlated, narrowband channels for potential use in increased-capacity quantum networks.

articleTitle: Efficient single-photon counting at 1.55 /spl mu/m via frequency upconversion
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We have achieved efficient single-photon detection at 1.55 /spl mu/m by sum-frequency mixing with a strong cw pump at 1064 nm in periodically-poled lithium niobate and subsequent single-photon counting in the visible.

articleTitle: Resolution and apodization in images generated by twin photons
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A theoretical study on the image formation of an object when illuminated by at least one of the photons generated by the process of spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is discussed. Image is detected in coincidence at the image plane by signal and idler detectors, after the idler photon is transmitted through the object. Simulation results on the comparison between coincidence rate and the classical light intensity at the image plane are presented. Simulations show that the image obtained with the parametric down-converted light source is better resolved than the one obtained with infrared classical source, but not equal to the resolution of the image produced by the violet classical light source. The presence of a strong apodization in the quantum image is also noticed, due to the existence of the effective nonlocal lens.

articleTitle: Waveguide-plasmon polaritons in a 1D metallic photonic crystal slab
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We study experimentally and theoretically the interaction of waveguide modes with nanowire plasmon resonances in a grating-waveguide structure. The coupling leads to the formation of a waveguide-plasmon polariton with a Rabi splitting of 250 meV.

articleTitle: Sub-Doppler cooling in a strontium magneto-optical trap
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: A systematic study of the sub-Doppler cooling in a strontium magneto-optical trap is presented. A detailed theoretical analysis of this system, based on a fully expanded multi-level theory, is also discussed. Furthermore, density-related radiation heating dynamics are found to play a crucial role in this system with reduced sub-Doppler cooling force.

articleTitle: Feedback control of soliton self-frequency shift and nonlinear loss in optical fibers
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We use adaptive feedback to control the amount of soliton Raman self-frequency shift in 100 meters of optical fiber. Phase-only pulse shaping at 1.55 /spl mu/m with a deformable mirror is used at the input.

articleTitle: Excitation of coherent phonons and plasmons in InSb by impulsive Raman scattering
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: The relative contributions of coherent phonons and plasmons in the THz emission spectra of InSb change with azimuthal orientation. This suggests interference of two Raman excitation processes.

articleTitle: Quantum noise in stochastic cooling of trapped atoms
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: Stochastic cooling of trapped atoms consists of the measurement of total momentum of part of the atoms in the trap and its subsequent compensation by giving the atoms a momentum kick. Both operations may be implemented by application of optical (laser) fields. The fraction of atoms affected is determined by the volume where atoms interact with the applied fields, i.e. the optical beam. This study identifies two sources of quantum noise in stochastic cooling that determine the ultimate cooling limit of the method. They appear as heating when considering the change of energy due to a single operation of stochastic cooling.

articleTitle: Absence of Bloch-Siegert shift and oscillation in optically excited microwave transitions
publicationTitle: Postconference Digest Quantum Electronics and Laser Science, 2003. QELS.
abstract: We show that even when the effective Rabi frequency is large compared to the transition frequency, a microwave transition excited by an optically off-resonant Raman transition is immune to Bloch-Siegert effect and oscillation.
